title: Temporal Entanglement in Quantum Field Theory
summary: In this paper I propose a branch point twist field approach to computing a temporal entropy, that is, an entanglement measure across different time regions, as opposed to the usual spacial measures. I discuss how the shift to time-dependence manifests in form factor calculations and how the generalization of the spacial measures to temporal ones reproduces expected features of the temporal entanglement: the entropy is complex, oscillatory and reminiscent of the evolution of entanglement following a global quench. Considering the temporal von Neumann entropy, I argue that spacial and temporal entropies are two sides of the same coin. They both encapsulate universal information about the theory, in particular its mass spectrum. Also in both cases, a quasiparticle picture can be employed to interpret results. Some qualitative features of this version of temporal entropy, such as its similarity to the entanglement entropy after a global quench, are shared with the known temporal measures.

AI.tldr: Proposes branch point twist field approach for computing temporal entanglement entropy across time regions, showing it yields complex oscillatory behavior similar to post-quench evolution.
AI.motivation: To extend entanglement measures from spatial to temporal domains and develop a formalism for computing temporal entanglement entropy using established integrable quantum field theory techniques.
AI.method: Uses branch point twist field approach adapted for temporal entanglement, analyzing how time-dependence manifests in form factor calculations and generalizing spatial measures to temporal ones.
AI.result: Temporal entropy is complex, oscillatory, and reminiscent of entanglement evolution following global quench; both spatial and temporal entropies encode universal information about theory's mass spectrum and admit quasiparticle interpretation.
AI.conclusion: Spatial and temporal entropies are complementary aspects of the same underlying structure, both capturing universal information about quantum field theories and sharing qualitative features with known temporal measures.

title: Thermodynamics and Geometrical Optics of Reissner Nordstrom de Sitter Black Holes in Noncommutative Geometry
summary: We investigate the thermodynamic, optical, and dynamical properties of Reissner-Nordstrom-de Sitter black holes in a noncommutative spacetime with a minimal length scale Theta. Within a two-horizon framework, we formulate an effective first law of thermodynamics and introduce an entropy capturing correlations between the event and cosmological horizons. Imposing the lukewarm condition, where both horizons share a common temperature, uniquely determines the entropy correction and yields closed-form expressions for thermodynamic quantities. The analysis reveals a noncommutativity-induced second-order phase transition, emphasizing the role of short-distance structure. On the optical side, we study photon motion and weak gravitational lensing, showing that noncommutativity modifies the effective potential and critical impact parameter. Using the Gauss-Bonnet method, we derive the weak deflection angle and analyze the effects of charge and cosmological constant. We further connect geometry and dynamics through the Lyapunov exponent and quasinormal modes, showing systematic impacts on orbital instability and damping.

AI.tldr: Noncommutative spacetime effects on Reissner-Nordstrom-de Sitter black holes: thermodynamic phase transitions, modified gravitational lensing, and connections between geometry and dynamics through Lyapunov exponents and quasinormal modes.
AI.motivation: To investigate how minimal length scale noncommutativity (Theta) modifies the properties of charged black holes in de Sitter spacetime, particularly focusing on thermodynamic behavior, optical phenomena, and dynamical stability.
AI.method: Two-horizon thermodynamic framework with effective first law; lukewarm condition for common temperature; Gauss-Bonnet method for weak deflection angle; analysis of photon motion, effective potential, Lyapunov exponents, and quasinormal modes.
AI.result: Noncommutativity induces second-order phase transition; modifies effective potential and critical impact parameter; yields closed-form thermodynamic expressions; systematically affects orbital instability and damping through Lyapunov exponents and quasinormal modes.
AI.conclusion: Noncommutative spacetime with minimal length scale significantly alters black hole thermodynamics, optics, and dynamics, revealing phase transitions and systematic modifications to gravitational lensing and stability properties.

title: Horizon Edge Partition Functions in $Λ>0$ Quantum Gravity
comment: 6 pages + appendix, 2 figures. Short PRL version of arXiv:2501.17912 and arXiv:2506.02142. Accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. Lett
summary: We obtain the spectra of codimension-2 horizon "edge" degrees of freedom for gravity and higher-spin gauge fields in de Sitter space and in the static Nariai spacetime, advancing previous Lorentzian and Euclidean analyses of one-loop thermodynamics. The edge spectra exhibit universal shift symmetries, revealing a novel symmetry-breaking structure in one-loop partition functions with positive cosmological constant. For the graviton, these modes admit a geometric interpretation as fluctuations of the cosmic horizon, which also persists in the Nariai case.

AI.tldr: Analysis of codimension-2 horizon edge degrees of freedom for gravity and higher-spin fields in de Sitter and Nariai spacetimes, revealing universal shift symmetries and novel symmetry-breaking in one-loop partition functions with positive cosmological constant.
AI.motivation: To advance previous Lorentzian and Euclidean analyses of one-loop thermodynamics by studying the spectra of codimension-2 horizon "edge" degrees of freedom for gravity and higher-spin gauge fields in cosmological spacetimes with positive cosmological constant.
AI.method: Analysis of edge spectra for gravity and higher-spin gauge fields in de Sitter space and static Nariai spacetime, examining universal shift symmetries and their implications for one-loop partition functions.
AI.result: Edge spectra exhibit universal shift symmetries revealing novel symmetry-breaking structure in one-loop partition functions with positive cosmological constant. For gravitons, these modes admit geometric interpretation as fluctuations of the cosmic horizon, persisting in the Nariai case.
AI.conclusion: The study advances understanding of one-loop thermodynamics in cosmological spacetimes by revealing universal shift symmetries in edge degrees of freedom and their geometric interpretation as horizon fluctuations, with implications for symmetry-breaking in quantum gravity with positive cosmological constant.

title: Inverse Electroweak Baryogenesis
summary: We propose a mechanism for baryogenesis in which the baryon asymmetry is generated as an \emph{equilibrium response} of weak sphalerons in a region where electroweak sphaleron transitions remain unsuppressed, $h/T\lesssim 1$. A nonzero equilibrium baryon density arises in the presence of an approximately conserved global charge $X$, carried by states with nonzero hypercharge and, after electroweak symmetry breaking, electric charge. Plasma screening enforces gauge-charge neutrality, so an $X$ asymmetry induces compensating gauge-charge densities in the Standard Model plasma, which in turn bias weak sphaleron transitions toward a state with nonvanishing baryon number. The required $X$ asymmetry is generated during a phase transition that changes the strength of electroweak symmetry breaking, but need not coincide with the final electroweak phase transition. In particular, the mechanism can operate during an inverse electroweak phase transition, where baryon number is produced behind the advancing wall, in contrast to conventional electroweak baryogenesis. Because baryon production is decoupled from a direct first-order electroweak phase transition, the scenario can be realized at parametrically higher temperatures than standard electroweak baryogenesis, thereby weakening current experimental constraints. This framework provides a qualitatively distinct route to electroweak baryogenesis, with different parametric dependence, phase-transition dynamics, and phenomenological signatures.

AI.tldr: Baryogenesis mechanism where baryon asymmetry emerges as equilibrium response of weak sphalerons in unsuppressed regime, decoupled from direct first-order electroweak phase transition.
AI.motivation: To develop a qualitatively distinct electroweak baryogenesis framework that operates at higher temperatures than conventional approaches, weakening experimental constraints and enabling baryon production during inverse phase transitions.
AI.method: Utilizes approximately conserved global charge X asymmetry to bias weak sphaleron transitions via plasma screening effects; baryon number generated as equilibrium response in regions where sphaleron transitions remain unsuppressed (h/T ≲ 1).
AI.result: Proposes mechanism where baryon asymmetry can be produced during inverse electroweak phase transitions (behind advancing wall), at parametrically higher temperatures than standard electroweak baryogenesis, with different parametric dependence and phase-transition dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Provides novel electroweak baryogenesis framework with distinct phenomenological signatures, enabling baryon production decoupled from direct first-order phase transitions and operating at higher temperatures to evade current experimental constraints.

title: Gaugings of Groupoids, Strings in Shadows, and Emergent Poisson $σ$-Models
summary: The gauge principle is proposed for rigid Lie-groupoidal symmetries $G=>M$ of the Polyakov-Alvarez-Gawędzki 2$d$ non-linear $σ$-model with metric target $(M,g_M)$ and the WZ term given by a CS differential character coming from an abelian gerbe $\mathcal{G}$. The principle bases on the notion of principaloid bundle with connection $(P,Θ)$, introduced by Strobl and the Author. The descent of the model to the shadow of $P$ is demonstrated to require a twisted $G$-equivariant structure on $\mathcal{G}$, prequantising a multiplicative extension $(H_M,ρ,0)$ of the gerbe's curvature $H_M$ to a 3-cocycle in the BSS cohomology of the groupoid's nerve. The descent is accompanied by a combined $g_M$-isometric/$ρ$-holonomic reduction of the structure group of $P$, and uses an augmentation of the original gerbe by a trivial one depending quadratically on $Θ$. The latter couples to the field of the $σ$-model -- in an extension of the scheme worked out for the action groupoid by Gawędzki, Waldorf and the Author -- through the comomentum component of the Spencer pair of $ρ$, as described by Crainic et al. A fully fledged cohomological analysis of the relevant gauge anomaly and of inequivalent gaugings is presented. In the symplectic setting, the augmentation procedure is shown to lead to the emergence of the standard Poisson $σ$-model. Conversely, a coaugmentation of a (local) Poisson $σ$-model by a flat equivariant gerbe yields a novel field theory with the shadow of the underlying symplectic principaloid bundle as the configuration bundle, and with manifest lagrangean gauge symmetry. A simple Cartan-type associating mechanism is proposed to account for the reduction of the structure group of the principaloid bundle. The mechanism allows for the coupling of an arbitrary number of distinct charged matter-field species to a given gauge field.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a gauge principle for rigid Lie-groupoidal symmetries in 2D sigma models with Wess-Zumino terms, using principaloid bundles and gerbes to achieve gauge descent and anomaly analysis, connecting to Poisson sigma models.
AI.motivation: To establish a gauge principle for rigid Lie-groupoidal symmetries in Polyakov-Alvarez-Gawędzki 2D nonlinear sigma models with Wess-Zumino terms, extending previous work on action groupoids and developing a comprehensive framework for gauge anomalies and inequivalent gaugings.
AI.method: Uses principaloid bundles with connection (P,Θ) introduced by Strobl and the author, requires twisted G-equivariant structure on abelian gerbes, employs augmentation of original gerbe by trivial one quadratic in Θ, and proposes Cartan-type associating mechanism for structure group reduction.
AI.result: Demonstrates descent to shadow of P requires twisted G-equivariant structure prequantizing multiplicative extension of gerbe curvature to 3-cocycle in BSS cohomology, shows augmentation leads to standard Poisson sigma model in symplectic setting, and develops cohomological analysis of gauge anomalies.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides comprehensive gauge principle for Lie-groupoidal symmetries, connects sigma models to Poisson sigma models through augmentation/coaugmentation procedures, enables coupling of multiple charged matter fields, and offers complete cohomological analysis of gauge anomalies and inequivalent gaugings.

title: Probing the Higgs Self-Coupling with an XFEL Compton $γγ$ Collider at $\sqrt{s} = 380$ GeV
summary: We present a study probing the Higgs self-coupling with the X-ray free-electron laser Compton $γγ$ Collider (XCC) concept. The analysis is performed considering the $γγ\to HH \to bb\overline{bb}$ channel, and results are then extrapolated to obtain a projection on the Higgs self-coupling sensitivity that ranges between 7% and 12%. An ensemble of boosted decision trees is trained to discriminate between signal and backgrounds, paired with a genetic algorithm optimizer to combine the final classifier outputs. This study suggests that an X-ray FEL-based $γγ$ collider is a powerful tool to probe the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking, complementary to $e^+e^-$ Higgs factories and future high-energy hadron colliders.

AI.tldr: Study probes Higgs self-coupling using X-ray FEL Compton γγ collider via γγ→HH→bb̅bb̅ channel, achieving 7-12% sensitivity with boosted decision trees and genetic algorithm optimization.
AI.motivation: To investigate the Higgs self-coupling as a crucial test of electroweak symmetry breaking mechanism, using X-ray free-electron laser Compton γγ collider as a complementary approach to e⁺e⁻ Higgs factories and future hadron colliders.
AI.method: Analyzed γγ→HH→bb̅bb̅ channel at XCC. Trained ensemble of boosted decision trees for signal-background discrimination, paired with genetic algorithm optimizer to combine classifier outputs for optimal sensitivity.
AI.result: Achieved Higgs self-coupling sensitivity projection ranging between 7% and 12% for the XCC concept, demonstrating its potential as a powerful tool for probing electroweak symmetry breaking.
AI.conclusion: X-ray FEL-based γγ collider is a powerful complementary tool to e⁺e⁻ Higgs factories and future high-energy hadron colliders for probing Higgs self-coupling and electroweak symmetry breaking mechanism.

title: Dynamical symmetries of the Calogero-Coulomb model
summary: We construct the dynamical symmetry of the quantum Calogero model with particle exchange in a confining Coulomb field. This symmetry is governed by the algebra $so(N+1,2)$, deformed by exchange (Dunkl) operators, with its invariant sector generated by the Dunkl angular momentum tensor and the modified Laplace-Runge-Lenz vector. The equidistant analogue of the Hamiltonian, with a linear spectrum, is expressed in terms of the conformal subalgebra $so(1,2)$. In addition, the wave functions of the Calogero-Coulomb Hamiltonian are classified into infinite-dimensional lowest-weight $so(1,2)$ multiplets.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs the dynamical symmetry algebra so(N+1,2) for the quantum Calogero model with particle exchange in a confining Coulomb field, deformed by Dunkl operators, and analyzes its invariant sectors and wave function classification.
AI.motivation: To establish the dynamical symmetry structure of the quantum Calogero model with particle exchange in a Coulomb field, extending symmetry analysis to systems with exchange interactions using Dunkl operator formalism.
AI.method: Construction of deformed so(N+1,2) algebra using Dunkl operators, identification of invariant sectors via Dunkl angular momentum tensor and modified Laplace-Runge-Lenz vector, and classification of wave functions into so(1,2) multiplets.
AI.result: Successfully derived the dynamical symmetry algebra so(N+1,2) deformed by Dunkl operators, expressed the equidistant analogue Hamiltonian with linear spectrum using conformal subalgebra so(1,2), and classified Calogero-Coulomb Hamiltonian wave functions into infinite-dimensional lowest-weight so(1,2) multiplets.
AI.conclusion: The quantum Calogero model with particle exchange in a confining Coulomb field possesses a rich dynamical symmetry structure governed by Dunkl-deformed so(N+1,2) algebra, enabling systematic classification of states and revealing connections between conformal symmetry and integrable systems with exchange interactions.

title: Additional TeV-Scale Particles Predicted by Quartification
summary: The LHC has failed to discover any new elementary particle since the Higgs boson completed the standard model in 2012, Here we adopt the attractive method of quiver gauge field theories to make predictions of additional particles which might be found at Run 4 of the upgraded LH-LHC scheduled to begin in 2030. We use an $SU(3)^4$ quiver gauge theory and exhaustively classify all possibilities according to how many of the added states shlep, meaning acquire a super-heavy Dirac mass. We arrive at four different choices, each of which suggests interesting positive outcomes for Run 4.

AI.tldr: The paper uses quiver gauge theories to predict new particles for LHC Run 4, analyzing SU(3)^4 models with different "shlep" states that acquire super-heavy Dirac masses.
AI.motivation: The LHC has not discovered new particles since the Higgs boson in 2012, creating a need for theoretical frameworks to predict what might be found in the upcoming Run 4 of the upgraded LHC starting in 2030.
AI.method: Uses quiver gauge field theories with an SU(3)^4 gauge structure, exhaustively classifying all possibilities based on how many added states "shlep" (acquire super-heavy Dirac masses).
AI.result: Identifies four distinct choices/models, each suggesting interesting positive outcomes for LHC Run 4 discoveries.
AI.conclusion: Quiver gauge theories provide a promising framework for predicting new particles at the upgraded LHC, with four specific models offering testable predictions for Run 4 starting in 2030.

title: Shape modes of \(\mathbb{C}P^1\) vortices
summary: In this paper we investigate the existence of internal modes of vortices in the gauged \(\mathbb{C}P^1\) sigma model. We develop a clean geometric formalism that highlights the symmetries of the Jacobi operator, obtained from the second variation of the energy functional. The formalism and subsequent results fundamentally rely on the Bogomol'nyi decomposition of the energy functional, and can therefore be extended to other models with such a decomposition. We prove the existence of at least one shape mode for a general \(\mathbb{C}P^1\) vortex solution on \(\mathbb{R}^2\), and find numerically the shape modes and corresponding frequencies of a radially symmetric vortex. A surprising result is that the shape mode eigenvalues are very close to the scattering threshold, suggesting weakly bound shape modes could be characteristic of the \(\mathbb{C}P^1\) model.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates internal modes (shape modes) of vortices in the gauged CP^1 sigma model, develops geometric formalism for Jacobi operator symmetries, proves existence of at least one shape mode for general CP^1 vortices, and finds numerically that shape mode eigenvalues are close to scattering threshold.
AI.motivation: To understand the existence and properties of internal modes (shape modes) of vortices in the gauged CP^1 sigma model, which are important for vortex dynamics and stability analysis.
AI.method: Develops a geometric formalism highlighting symmetries of the Jacobi operator from second variation of energy functional, relies on Bogomol'nyi decomposition, proves existence of shape modes analytically for general CP^1 vortices, and performs numerical analysis for radially symmetric vortices.
AI.result: Proves existence of at least one shape mode for general CP^1 vortex solutions on R^2; numerically finds shape modes and frequencies for radially symmetric vortices; discovers that shape mode eigenvalues are very close to scattering threshold.
AI.conclusion: The developed geometric formalism based on Bogomol'nyi decomposition is generalizable to other models; weakly bound shape modes near scattering threshold may be characteristic of the CP^1 model, with implications for vortex dynamics.

title: Causality and stability analysis of relativistic spin hydrodynamics: insights from a nonvanishing spin density background
summary: We investigate the stability and causality of relativistic spin hydrodynamics in the presence of a nonvanishing spin-density background, assuming that the spin chemical potential enters at leading order, $ω^{μν}\sim\mathcal{O}(1)$, and remains finite in the linear perturbation analysis. It is found that within the first-order spin hydrodynamic framework, a finite spin-density background modifies the dispersion relations, and modes propagating along different directions are controlled by distinct transport coefficients. Certain specific modes only appear in the $x$-direction. However, the modes in the large wave-vector limit exhibit acausal behavior. To address this issue, we subsequently adopt the framework of minimal causal spin hydrodynamics and derive the corresponding stability and causality conditions. The spin density background directly determines whether stability and causality can be satisfied simultaneously. In the small wave-vector limit, the results are similar to those of the first-order theory. In the large wave-vector region, however, significant differences emerge: the distinctions between different directions are no longer merely simple substitutions of transport coefficients, but involve more complex combinations. This indicates that the difference between modes in different directions increases with increasing wave-vector.

AI.tldr: Relativistic spin hydrodynamics with finite spin-density background shows acausal behavior in first-order theory, which is resolved using minimal causal spin hydrodynamics framework with direction-dependent stability and causality conditions.
AI.motivation: To investigate stability and causality issues in relativistic spin hydrodynamics when a nonvanishing spin-density background exists, particularly addressing acausal behavior in large wave-vector limits of first-order theory.
AI.method: Two approaches: 1) First-order spin hydrodynamic framework with finite spin-density background, 2) Minimal causal spin hydrodynamics framework to address causality issues. Linear perturbation analysis with spin chemical potential ω^{μν}∼O(1).
AI.result: First-order theory shows modified dispersion relations with direction-dependent transport coefficients, specific modes only in x-direction, but exhibits acausal behavior in large wave-vector limit. Minimal causal framework resolves causality issues, with spin density background determining simultaneous satisfaction of stability and causality. Directional differences increase with wave-vector.
AI.conclusion: Finite spin-density background significantly affects relativistic spin hydrodynamics stability and causality. First-order theory fails in large wave-vector regime due to acausality, while minimal causal spin hydrodynamics provides consistent framework with direction-dependent behavior that intensifies with increasing wave-vector.

title: Euclidean E-models
summary:
We study a class of E-models, referred to as Euclidean E-models, in which the operator E acting on the Drinfeld double squares to minus the identity rather than to the identity. This modification leads to significant structural differences from the standard E-model framework. Most notably, the sigma-models naturally associated with these E-models possess a Euclidean world-sheet.
  Although, for some Drinfeld doubles, every Lorentzian E-model admits a natural Euclidean counterpart, the duality, integrability, and renormalization properties of Euclidean E-models are independent of the Lorentzian case and must be studied separately.
  We illustrate the general constructions using the example of a Euclidean bi-Yang-Baxter deformation.

AI.tldr: Euclidean E-models are a variant where operator E squares to -1 instead of +1, leading to sigma-models with Euclidean world-sheets, requiring independent study of duality, integrability, and renormalization properties.
AI.motivation: To study a modified class of E-models where the operator E acting on the Drinfeld double squares to minus the identity rather than the identity, which leads to significant structural differences from standard E-models and naturally produces sigma-models with Euclidean world-sheets.
AI.method: Analysis of Euclidean E-models defined by the condition E² = -1 on the Drinfeld double, investigation of their structural properties, and examination of duality, integrability, and renormalization aspects separately from Lorentzian counterparts. Illustration using the example of Euclidean bi-Yang-Baxter deformation.
AI.result: Euclidean E-models produce sigma-models with Euclidean world-sheets, and while some Drinfeld doubles allow natural Euclidean counterparts to Lorentzian E-models, their duality, integrability, and renormalization properties must be studied independently.
AI.conclusion: Euclidean E-models represent a distinct class with fundamentally different properties from standard Lorentzian E-models, requiring separate investigation of their theoretical framework and applications, as demonstrated through the Euclidean bi-Yang-Baxter deformation example.

title: Reheating Effects on Charged Lepton Yukawa Equilibration and Leptogenesis
comment: Contribution to CORFU2025: Workshop on the Standard Model and Beyond, 14 pages, 2 figures
summary: We show that accounting for a non-instantaneous reheating phase after inflation can significantly modify the charged lepton Yukawa equilibration temperature in the early Universe. This finding calls for revisiting the role of lepton flavors in leptogenesis models where right-handed neutrinos are produced and decay during the extended reheating period. Our analysis reveals that this effect can induce shifts in the flavor regime(s) of leptogenesis relative to standard scenario.

AI.tldr: Non-instantaneous reheating after inflation alters charged lepton Yukawa equilibration temperatures, requiring reevaluation of lepton flavor roles in leptogenesis during extended reheating periods.
AI.motivation: Standard leptogenesis scenarios typically assume instantaneous reheating after inflation, but realistic reheating is non-instantaneous and extended, which may significantly affect charged lepton Yukawa equilibration temperatures and consequently the flavor dynamics in leptogenesis.
AI.method: The authors analyze the impact of a non-instantaneous reheating phase on charged lepton Yukawa equilibration temperatures, examining how this extended reheating period affects right-handed neutrino production and decay dynamics in leptogenesis models.
AI.result: Accounting for non-instantaneous reheating significantly modifies charged lepton Yukawa equilibration temperatures, leading to shifts in the flavor regime(s) of leptogenesis relative to standard instantaneous reheating scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The extended reheating phase after inflation has important implications for leptogenesis, necessitating revisiting the role of lepton flavors in models where right-handed neutrinos are produced and decay during this period, as it can alter the flavor dynamics of leptogenesis.

title: Holographic One-Point Function and Geodesics in SdS$_3$
summary: Grinberg-Maldacena showed that, for AdS/CFT, the thermal one-point function of a heavy boundary operator in the dual conformal field theory encodes the complex geodesic length from the boundary insertion to the black hole singularity. We show that for an appropriate choice of bulk-boundary kernel, an analogous result holds for three-dimensional Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole. We prove the result for the case where SdS$_3$ has a finite orbifold group.

AI.tldr: The paper extends Grinberg-Maldacena's AdS/CFT result about thermal one-point functions encoding complex geodesic lengths to Schwarzschild-de Sitter black holes in three dimensions.
AI.motivation: To generalize the AdS/CFT correspondence result by Grinberg-Maldacena (which relates thermal one-point functions of heavy boundary operators to complex geodesic lengths from boundary to black hole singularity) to the Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime context.
AI.method: Using an appropriate choice of bulk-boundary kernel and proving the result specifically for three-dimensional Schwarzschild-de Sitter black holes with finite orbifold groups.
AI.result: Demonstrates that an analogous result holds for SdS$_3$: the thermal one-point function of a heavy boundary operator encodes the complex geodesic length from boundary insertion to the black hole singularity, when using the appropriate bulk-boundary kernel.
AI.conclusion: The Grinberg-Maldacena correspondence between thermal one-point functions and complex geodesic lengths can be extended beyond AdS/CFT to include Schwarzschild-de Sitter black holes in three dimensions, at least for cases with finite orbifold groups.

title: Searching for the Proton's Missing Spin: Small-$x$ Helicity Evolution Equations and Their Analytic Solutions
summary:
The proton spin puzzle denotes the challenge of describing the proton's spin in terms of the angular momenta of the quarks and gluons which comprise it. These quarks and gluons carry a fraction $x$ of the proton's momentum. Contributions from small-$x$ quarks and gluons, which only possess a little of the proton's momentum, are difficult to measure, since this requires very high energy experiments. Furthermore, early theoretical work in the 1990s predicted substantial contributions to the proton spin from these small-$x$ particles. We need theoretical control over this corner of phase space in order to resolve the spin puzzle.
  In this dissertation, we build upon an existing framework for studying spin at small-$x$. Previously, several sets of small-$x$ evolution equations were derived in this formalism -- one in the large-$N_c$ limit and one in the large-$N_c\&N_f$ limit. Here $N_c$ and $N_f$ are the numbers of quark colors and flavors. These equations were numerically solved but no analytic solutions had been found. In this dissertation we detail the construction of such analytic solutions, first in the large-$N_c$ limit and then in the large-$N_c\&N_f$ limit, after deriving an important correction to the existing large-$N_c\&N_f$ equations due to the contributions of quark-to-gluon transition operators.
  From the solutions constructed here, we can predict the behavior of the quark and gluon helicity distributions at asymptotically small-$x$ (and large-$N_c$ or large-$N_c\&N_f$), both as a general power law and further as explicit analytic expressions in the asymptotic limit. Our solutions also allow us to predict all four polarized DGLAP anomalous dimensions in the same limits, yielding expressions exact to all orders in the strong coupling. The expansions of our predictions agree completely with the full extent of existing finite-order calculations, to three loops.

AI.tldr: This dissertation provides analytic solutions for small-x evolution equations in the proton spin puzzle, enabling predictions for quark/gluon helicity distributions and polarized DGLAP anomalous dimensions in large-Nc and large-Nc&Nf limits.
AI.motivation: The proton spin puzzle requires understanding contributions from small-x quarks and gluons, which are difficult to measure experimentally and were predicted to contribute substantially to proton spin. Theoretical control over this phase space region is needed to resolve the puzzle.
AI.method: Building on existing small-x spin formalism, the work constructs analytic solutions for evolution equations: first in the large-Nc limit, then in the large-Nc&Nf limit after deriving important corrections to existing equations due to quark-to-gluon transition operators.
AI.result: The analytic solutions predict the asymptotic behavior of quark and gluon helicity distributions at small-x (in large-Nc or large-Nc&Nf limits) as power laws and explicit analytic expressions. They also yield all four polarized DGLAP anomalous dimensions exactly to all orders in strong coupling, with expansions agreeing completely with existing three-loop calculations.
AI.conclusion: The dissertation provides crucial theoretical tools for understanding small-x contributions to proton spin through analytic solutions of evolution equations, enabling predictions for helicity distributions and anomalous dimensions that bridge the gap between numerical solutions and perturbative calculations.

title: Symmetries of non-maximal supergravities with higher-derivative corrections
summary: We consider hidden symmetries arising from U-duality in the dimensional reduction of non-maximal higher-derivative supergravities to three dimensions. In particular, we consider the $G_{2(2)}$ symmetry of minimal five-dimensional supergravity and the $O(d+p+1,d+1)$ symmetry of bosonic and heterotic string theory on $T^d$. Using a group theory argument, we show that the higher-derivative corrections explicitly break all hidden symmetry enhancements. As special cases, this also implies that higher-derivative corrections prevent the symmetry enhancement to $SL(3,\mathbb R)$ in pure five-dimensional gravity and $O(4,4)$ in the STU model.

AI.tldr: Higher-derivative corrections in non-maximal supergravities explicitly break all hidden symmetry enhancements arising from U-duality in dimensional reduction to three dimensions.
AI.motivation: To understand how higher-derivative corrections affect hidden symmetries that emerge from U-duality when non-maximal supergravities are dimensionally reduced to three dimensions.
AI.method: Using group theory arguments to analyze the $G_{2(2)}$ symmetry of minimal five-dimensional supergravity and the $O(d+p+1,d+1)$ symmetry of bosonic and heterotic string theory on $T^d$.
AI.result: Higher-derivative corrections explicitly break all hidden symmetry enhancements, including the enhancement to $SL(3,\mathbb R)$ in pure five-dimensional gravity and $O(4,4)$ in the STU model.
AI.conclusion: Hidden symmetries that appear in the classical limit of supergravity theories are generically broken by higher-derivative corrections, preventing symmetry enhancement in the presence of quantum corrections.

title: Elastic proton-proton and pion-proton scattering in holographic QCD
comment: 11 pages, 7 figures, prepared for the proceedings of the XXXVII International Workshop on High Energy Physics: "Diffraction of hadrons: Experiment, Theory, Phenomenology" (HEPFT2025), 22-24 July 2025, Protvino, Russia
summary: The elastic proton-proton and pion-proton scattering processes are investigated in the framework of holographic QCD. Considering the Pomeron and Reggeon exchange in the Regge regime, the total and differential cross sections are calculated. In the model setup, the Pomeron and Reggeon exchange are described by the Reggeized spin-2 glueball and vector meson propagator, respectively. For the differential cross sections, contributions of the Coulomb interaction are also taken into account. Adjustable parameters involved in the model are determined with the experimental data, and it is presented that the resulting cross sections are consistent with the data in a wide kinematic region.

AI.tldr: Holographic QCD model describes elastic proton-proton and pion-proton scattering via Pomeron and Reggeon exchanges, calculating total and differential cross sections consistent with experimental data.
AI.motivation: To investigate elastic proton-proton and pion-proton scattering processes using holographic QCD framework, addressing the need for theoretical descriptions of hadronic scattering in the Regge regime that can match experimental data across wide kinematic regions.
AI.method: Uses holographic QCD framework with Pomeron exchange modeled by Reggeized spin-2 glueball propagator and Reggeon exchange by vector meson propagator. Includes Coulomb interaction contributions for differential cross sections. Model parameters are determined by fitting to experimental data.
AI.result: The model successfully reproduces both total and differential cross sections for elastic proton-proton and pion-proton scattering, showing consistency with experimental data across wide kinematic regions after parameter optimization.
AI.conclusion: Holographic QCD provides a viable framework for describing hadronic scattering processes, with Pomeron and Reggeon exchanges effectively modeled by Reggeized spin-2 glueball and vector meson propagators, respectively, yielding results consistent with experimental observations.

title: The Carrollian Superplane and Supersymmetry
summary: This note provides an intrinsic construction of the Carrollian superplane $Π\mathbb{S}\simeq \mathbb{R}^{2|4}$ as a supermanifold generalisation of the Carrollian plane. Moving away from the $c\rightarrow 0$ limit of relativistic spinors, we define Carroll spinors as sections of a degenerate Clifford module. We show that the Carrollian superplane is a principal $\mathbb{R}^{1|2}$-bundle. Once clock forms and a complementary basic one-form are specified, there is a pair of odd vector fields that generate novel $N =2$ Carrollian supersymmetry transformations, not all of which come from an Inönü--Wigner contraction of a Poincaré superalgebra

AI.tldr: Intrinsic construction of Carrollian superplane Π𝕊≃ℝ²|⁴ as supermanifold generalization of Carrollian plane, defining Carroll spinors via degenerate Clifford modules, showing it's a principal ℝ¹|²-bundle, with novel N=2 Carrollian supersymmetry transformations from specified clock forms.
AI.motivation: To provide an intrinsic construction of Carrollian superplane without relying on c→0 limit of relativistic spinors, developing proper mathematical framework for Carroll spinors as sections of degenerate Clifford modules, and establishing novel Carrollian supersymmetry transformations not derivable from Inönü-Wigner contraction.
AI.method: Construct Carrollian superplane Π𝕊≃ℝ²|⁴ as supermanifold, define Carroll spinors as sections of degenerate Clifford module, demonstrate it's a principal ℝ¹|²-bundle, specify clock forms and complementary basic one-form to derive odd vector fields generating N=2 Carrollian supersymmetry transformations.
AI.result: Successfully constructed intrinsic Carrollian superplane, defined Carroll spinors via degenerate Clifford modules, proved Carrollian superplane is principal ℝ¹|²-bundle, identified novel N=2 Carrollian supersymmetry transformations not obtainable from Inönü-Wigner contraction of Poincaré superalgebra.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes intrinsic mathematical framework for Carrollian superplane and Carroll spinors, revealing novel supersymmetry structures in Carrollian geometry that go beyond simple contractions of relativistic theories, opening new directions in Carrollian supersymmetry research.

title: Thermal modification of $K_1(1270)\to π^+π^-K^+$ in a hot hadronic medium
summary: We study the thermal modification of the exclusive decay $K_1^+(1270)\to π^+π^-K^+$ in a hot hadronic medium. The decay amplitude is constructed from effective hadronic interactions dominated by the $ρ$- and $K^*$-pole contributions, which enables a Dalitz-level analysis of the three-body decay in medium. Thermal effects associated with partial chiral-symmetry restoration are incorporated through a phenomenological interpolation toward vector--axial-vector degeneracy near the chiral crossover. As the temperature increases, the reduction of the parent $K_1$ mass strongly compresses the available three-body phase space, leading to substantial deformation of the Dalitz distribution and invariant-mass spectra, as well as to a pronounced suppression of $Γ_{K_1\toπ^+π^-K^+}(T)$. As a further step toward future experimental comparison, we introduce normalized shape observables that quantify the thermal evolution of the $K^*$-dominated $πK$ region, the upper-edge weight of the $ππ$ spectrum, and the compactification of the Dalitz population. The dominant effect identified in the present framework is therefore kinematic: thermal phase-space reduction in the strange axial-vector channel. These results suggest that the exclusive $K_1(1270)$ channel may provide a useful qualitative probe of in-medium strange axial-vector dynamics near the pseudocritical region.

AI.tldr: Thermal modification of exclusive decay K₁⁺(1270)→π⁺π⁻K⁺ in hot hadronic medium shows strong kinematic suppression due to phase-space compression from reduced parent mass, with deformed Dalitz distributions and normalized shape observables proposed for experimental comparison.
AI.motivation: To study how thermal effects in a hot hadronic medium modify the exclusive decay of strange axial-vector meson K₁(1270) to three-body final state, particularly focusing on phase-space changes due to partial chiral-symmetry restoration effects near the chiral crossover temperature.
AI.method: Construct decay amplitude from effective hadronic interactions dominated by ρ- and K*-pole contributions, enabling Dalitz-level analysis. Incorporate thermal effects through phenomenological interpolation toward vector-axial-vector degeneracy near chiral crossover, accounting for temperature-dependent parent mass reduction.
AI.result: Increasing temperature reduces parent K₁ mass, strongly compressing available three-body phase space, leading to substantial deformation of Dalitz distribution and invariant-mass spectra, and pronounced suppression of decay width. Normalized shape observables quantify thermal evolution of K*-dominated πK region, upper-edge weight of ππ spectrum, and Dalitz population compactification.
AI.conclusion: Dominant effect is kinematic: thermal phase-space reduction in strange axial-vector channel. Exclusive K₁(1270) channel may serve as useful qualitative probe of in-medium strange axial-vector dynamics near pseudocritical region, with proposed observables enabling future experimental comparison.

title: Light-cone Distribution Amplitudes of Vector Mesons within the Self-Consistent Light-front Quark Model
summary: In this paper, we investigate the twist-2 and twist-3 light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of vector mesons within the light-front quark model, and the $n$th Gegenbauer moment $a_n(μ)$, $ξ$-moment $\langle ξ^n\rangle^{\parallel(\perp)}$ and transverse moment $\langle \mathbf{k}^n_\perp\rangle^{\parallel(\perp)}$ are also carried out. Adopting the parameter set fixed by confinements from the mesonic decay constants, we perform the numerical analysis and the results reveal several key insights: (i) The flavor symmetry breaking effects are more pronounced in the twist-3 LCDAs of vector mesons, which leads to the establishment of $a_1^\perp>a_1^\parallel$ and $\langle ξ^n\rangle^\perp>\langle ξ^n\rangle^\parallel$. This consists with previous findings in research for the LCDAs of pseudoscalar mesons. (ii) For vector mesons, the twist dependence decreases in the heavy quark limit which lead to $φ_{2}^\parallel(x)\simeqφ_{3}^\perp(x)$. For pseudoscalar and vector mesons composed of the same quark constituents, their LCDAs with the same twist exhibit similarity and gradually converge as the increasing of quark mass, i.e., $φ_{2}^A(x)\simeqφ_{2}^\parallel(x)$ and $φ_{3}^P(x)\simeqφ_{3}^\perp(x)$ in $m_q\rightarrow\infty$. This reveals the spin independence of LCDAs in the heavy quark limit. Furthermore, it is found $φ^A_2(x)\simeqφ_2^\parallel(x)\approxφ_3^P(x)\simeqφ_3^\perp(x)$ with the replacement $M\rightarrow M_0$ and in the heavy quark limit.

AI.tldr: The paper studies twist-2 and twist-3 light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of vector mesons using a light-front quark model, calculating Gegenbauer moments, ξ-moments, and transverse moments, revealing flavor symmetry breaking effects and heavy quark limit behavior.
AI.motivation: To investigate the twist-2 and twist-3 light-cone distribution amplitudes of vector mesons within the light-front quark model framework, and to understand flavor symmetry breaking effects and heavy quark limit behavior in meson LCDAs.
AI.method: Using light-front quark model with parameter set fixed by mesonic decay constants, calculating nth Gegenbauer moments a_n(μ), ξ-moments ⟨ξ^n⟩^(∥,⊥), and transverse moments ⟨k_⊥^n⟩^(∥,⊥) for vector mesons.
AI.result: (i) Flavor symmetry breaking effects are more pronounced in twist-3 LCDAs, establishing a_1^⊥ > a_1^∥ and ⟨ξ^n⟩^⊥ > ⟨ξ^n⟩^∥. (ii) Twist dependence decreases in heavy quark limit leading to φ_2^∥(x) ≃ φ_3^⊥(x). (iii) LCDAs of pseudoscalar and vector mesons with same quark constituents converge in heavy quark limit, showing spin independence: φ_2^A(x) ≃ φ_2^∥(x) and φ_3^P(x) ≃ φ_3^⊥(x).
AI.conclusion: The study reveals important patterns in vector meson LCDAs: significant flavor symmetry breaking in twist-3 components, reduced twist dependence in heavy quark limit, and convergence between pseudoscalar and vector meson LCDAs demonstrating spin independence in heavy quark systems.

title: Three-loop functions for a quartic model with a cutoff
comment: LaTeX, 7 pages. Firstly appeared in Russian, March 16, 2026, see https://www.pdmi.ras.ru/preprint/2026/26-02.html
summary: This paper presents numerical values for auxiliary integrals and coefficients of the beta function in the three-loop approximation for a four-dimensional model with a quartic interaction, using a special type of regularization function. The values are compared to previously obtained results.

AI.tldr: Three-loop beta function coefficients and auxiliary integrals computed for 4D quartic interaction model using special regularization; results compared to prior work.
AI.motivation: To provide precise numerical values for auxiliary integrals and beta function coefficients at three-loop order in a four-dimensional quartic interaction model, using a specific regularization scheme, and validate against existing results.
AI.method: Numerical computation using a special type of regularization function for the three-loop approximation in a four-dimensional model with quartic interaction.
AI.result: Numerical values obtained for auxiliary integrals and beta function coefficients; comparison shows agreement or discrepancies with previously published results.
AI.conclusion: The computed numerical values provide verification and reference for three-loop calculations in quartic field theories, confirming consistency with or identifying differences from earlier work.

title: Solving Functional Renormalization Group Equations with Neural Networks
summary: We employ deep neural networks to represent the field derivative of the scale-dependent effective potential in the functional renormalization group (fRG) framework for nonperturbative quantum field theory. By embedding the fRG flow equations directly into the loss function, the network parameters are determined so as to provide a continuous and differentiable representation of the scale- and field-dependent effective potential without relying on precomputed training data. Focusing on the $O(N)$ scalar field theory within the local potential approximation at finite temperature, we demonstrate that this neural network representation accurately captures the renormalization group flow across symmetric, broken, and critical regimes. A key ingredient is a decomposition of the representation into an analytically known large-$N$ contribution and a learned finite-$N$ correction, which efficiently mitigates numerical stiffness associated with convexity restoration in the broken phase. The physics-driven solutions show excellent agreement with established finite-difference and discontinuous Galerkin methods. We further apply the same strategy to the Wilson-Fisher fixed point equation in three dimensions, illustrating that neural network representations provide a unified framework for both scale-dependent flows and fixed-point problems. Our results indicate that physics-driven deep learning offers a robust and flexible numerical tool for functional renormalization group studies.

AI.tldr: Neural networks represent effective potential in functional renormalization group, solving flow equations directly via physics-driven learning without training data, applied to O(N) scalar theory and Wilson-Fisher fixed point.
AI.motivation: Develop a robust numerical framework for functional renormalization group (fRG) studies using deep learning to overcome limitations of traditional numerical methods, particularly addressing numerical stiffness in convexity restoration during broken phase transitions.
AI.method: Embed fRG flow equations directly into neural network loss functions to learn scale- and field-dependent effective potentials without precomputed data. Use decomposition into analytical large-N contribution plus learned finite-N correction to mitigate numerical stiffness. Apply to O(N) scalar theory in local potential approximation at finite temperature.
AI.result: Neural network accurately captures RG flow across symmetric, broken, and critical regimes, showing excellent agreement with finite-difference and discontinuous Galerkin methods. Successfully applied to Wilson-Fisher fixed point in 3D, demonstrating unified framework for scale-dependent flows and fixed-point problems.
AI.conclusion: Physics-driven deep learning provides flexible, robust numerical tool for fRG studies, capable of handling challenging regimes like convexity restoration and offering unified approach for both flow equations and fixed-point problems.

title: Self-dual gravity from higher-spin theory
summary: Higher-spin symmetry is known to mix lower-spin fields with higher-spin fields, creating a complex interaction picture where no closed finite field sector is expected to exist for dimensions greater than three. By studying the self-dual part of higher-spin interaction vertices in four dimensions, we show that gauge fields of spins greater than two can be consistently set to zero. In this case, the fields with helicities $-2\leqλ\leq 0$ form a closed sub-sector and also act as sources for positive helicities. For these lower spin fields, we identify their equations of motion. In particular, we show that self-dual gravity with a cosmological constant emerges as a unique rigid part of higher-spin interactions. Notably, its equations have a form that incorporates the Moyal star product, which is essential for generating the higher-spin algebra. Therefore, we demonstrate that self-dual gravity can be derived from higher-spin symmetries.

AI.tldr: Self-dual gravity emerges as a rigid part of higher-spin interactions in four dimensions, with fields of spins greater than two consistently set to zero, forming a closed sub-sector of helicities -2≤λ≤0.
AI.motivation: Higher-spin symmetry creates complex interactions where no closed finite field sector exists for dimensions >3, motivating investigation of whether consistent sub-sectors can be isolated.
AI.method: Study self-dual part of higher-spin interaction vertices in four dimensions, set gauge fields of spins >2 to zero, analyze resulting closed sub-sector of helicities -2≤λ≤0, identify equations of motion.
AI.result: Fields with helicities -2≤λ≤0 form a closed sub-sector and act as sources for positive helicities; self-dual gravity with cosmological constant emerges as unique rigid part of higher-spin interactions, with equations incorporating Moyal star product.
AI.conclusion: Self-dual gravity can be derived from higher-spin symmetries, demonstrating that consistent sub-sectors exist despite the general complexity of higher-spin interactions in four dimensions.

title: Leptogenesis in the littlest inverse seesaw model
summary: The littlest inverse seesaw (LIS) model represents the first low-scale seesaw framework to successfully account for all six physical observables of the neutrino sector with merely two effective free parameters, making it highly worthy of in-depth investigation. In this work, we investigate realizations of leptogenesis in this framework. We consider two distinct scenarios. In the first, the two pseudo-Dirac sterile neutrino pairs are initially exactly degenerate and subsequently acquire small mass splittings via the RGE effects, enabling resonant leptogenesis to occur across different PD pairs and consequently enhancing leptogenesis. In the second, the two PD pairs feature a hierarchical mass spectrum, and leptogenesis proceeds via sterile neutrino oscillations through the ARS mechanism. We show that the observed baryon asymmetry can be successfully reproduced in sizable regions of the parameter space without introducing additional free parameters, demonstrating that the LIS framework provides a viable and predictive setting for low-scale leptogenesis.

AI.tldr: The LIS model explains neutrino physics with just two parameters; this paper explores leptogenesis in two scenarios: resonant leptogenesis via RGE-induced mass splittings in degenerate pseudo-Dirac pairs, and hierarchical ARS mechanism via sterile neutrino oscillations.
AI.motivation: The littlest inverse seesaw (LIS) model successfully accounts for all six neutrino observables with only two effective free parameters, making it worthy of deeper investigation for leptogenesis possibilities.
AI.method: Two distinct leptogenesis scenarios: 1) Initially degenerate pseudo-Dirac sterile neutrino pairs acquire small mass splittings via RGE effects, enabling resonant leptogenesis across different pairs; 2) Hierarchical mass spectrum with leptogenesis via sterile neutrino oscillations through the ARS mechanism.
AI.result: The observed baryon asymmetry can be successfully reproduced in sizable regions of the parameter space without introducing additional free parameters.
AI.conclusion: The LIS framework provides a viable and predictive setting for low-scale leptogenesis, demonstrating compatibility with both neutrino physics and baryogenesis requirements.

title: Covariant Symplectic Geometry of Classical Particles
summary: We investigate the tension between symplecticity and gauge covariance in classical Hamiltonian mechanics. The pursuit of manifest covariance over manifest symplecticity results in a unique geometric formulation. Firstly, covariant yet non-canonical coordinates are employed by adopting Souriau's approach to minimal coupling. Secondly, covariant yet non-coordinate frames arise from Ehresmann connections in phase space. Thirdly, the concept of covariant Poisson bracket is introduced, facilitating direct derivations of covariant equations of motion. In this way, we establish manifestly covariant Hamiltonian formulations of particles coupled to background gauge and gravitational fields, with or without spin. The variational principle and path integral origins of our framework are also explicated.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a manifestly covariant Hamiltonian formulation for particles coupled to gauge and gravitational fields by prioritizing gauge covariance over symplecticity, using Souriau's minimal coupling, Ehresmann connections, and covariant Poisson brackets.
AI.motivation: To resolve the tension between symplecticity (canonical structure) and gauge covariance in classical Hamiltonian mechanics, particularly for particles coupled to background gauge and gravitational fields with or without spin.
AI.method: Three main approaches: 1) Using covariant but non-canonical coordinates via Souriau's minimal coupling; 2) Employing covariant but non-coordinate frames from Ehresmann connections in phase space; 3) Introducing covariant Poisson brackets for direct derivation of covariant equations of motion.
AI.result: Established manifestly covariant Hamiltonian formulations for particles coupled to background gauge and gravitational fields, with explicit connections to variational principles and path integral origins.
AI.conclusion: By prioritizing manifest covariance over manifest symplecticity, the paper achieves a unique geometric formulation that successfully reconciles Hamiltonian mechanics with gauge covariance requirements for field-coupled systems.

title: From pseudo-Dirac catastrophe to trimaximal mixing: why $A_4$ is the minimal resolution of the $Z_3$ neutrino failure
summary: We investigate whether the type-I seesaw mechanism can rescue the $Z_3$ Froggatt--Nielsen framework for neutrinos and find that it cannot. With right-handed Majorana masses carrying the $Z_3$ charge structure dictated by the Majorana bilinear -- where suppression powers follow $(q_i+q_j)\bmod 3$ -- the mass matrix contains an unsuppressed off-diagonal entry that creates a pseudo-Dirac pair among the heavy neutrinos. This forces $m_1\approx m_2$ in the light spectrum, suppressing the solar-to-atmospheric mass ratio to a median $Δm^2_{21}/Δm^2_{31}\sim 4\times 10^{-11}$ -- eight orders of magnitude below the observed value of $0.030$. We prove this failure is universal across all six permutations of the charges $(2,1,0)$ and show analytically that the generic ratio scales as $Δm^2_{21}/Δm^2_{31}\sim\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^5)\sim 10^{-9}$, with fewer than $0.01\%$ of parameter-space points exceeding $\varepsilon^2\approx 2\times 10^{-4}$. The PMNS angles remain Haar-random, carrying no information from the expansion parameter. We then show that $A_4$, the alternating group of order 12, is the minimal discrete symmetry resolving both failures. Its triplet representation provides two independent vacuum parameters controlling the solar and atmospheric mass scales separately, while constraining the PMNS matrix to the trimaximal TM$_1$ pattern. The TM$_1$ solar sum rule predicts $\sin^2θ_{12}=0.318$ ($1.2σ$ from NuFit 6.0, $1.0σ$ from JUNO), and the atmospheric sum rule yields a parameter-free $(\sin^2θ_{23},\,\cosδ)$ correlation predicting $δ\approx -71^\circ$, testable at DUNE and T2HK.

AI.tldr: The type-I seesaw mechanism fails to rescue the Z₃ Froggatt-Nielsen framework for neutrinos due to an unsuppressed off-diagonal entry creating a pseudo-Dirac pair, forcing m₁≈m₂ and suppressing Δm²₂₁/Δm²₃₁ by ~8 orders of magnitude below observed values. The minimal discrete symmetry A₄ resolves both failures, providing independent solar/atmospheric mass scale control and predicting TM₁ pattern with testable predictions for θ₁₂ and δ.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the type-I seesaw mechanism can rescue the Z₃ Froggatt-Nielsen framework for neutrinos, which faces challenges in reproducing observed neutrino mass ratios and mixing patterns.
AI.method: Analyzed the Z₃ Froggatt-Nielsen framework with type-I seesaw mechanism, examining charge structures and suppression patterns. Proved universal failure across all six permutations of charges (2,1,0). Then explored A₄ (alternating group of order 12) as minimal discrete symmetry solution, using its triplet representation with independent vacuum parameters.
AI.result: Type-I seesaw fails: creates pseudo-Dirac pair forcing m₁≈m₂, suppressing Δm²₂₁/Δm²₃₁ to median ~4×10⁻¹¹ (8 orders below observed 0.030). Generic ratio scales as O(ε⁵)~10⁻⁹, with <0.01% exceeding ε²≈2×10⁻⁴. A₄ resolves both failures: provides independent solar/atmospheric mass scale control, constrains PMNS to TM₁ pattern predicting sin²θ₁₂=0.318 and δ≈-71°.
AI.conclusion: The type-I seesaw cannot rescue the Z₃ Froggatt-Nielsen framework due to fundamental structural issues creating pseudo-Dirac pairs and suppressing mass ratios. A₄ emerges as the minimal discrete symmetry that resolves both mass ratio and mixing pattern failures, providing testable predictions for neutrino oscillation parameters through TM₁ sum rules.

title: A Note on the Perturbative Expansion of the Schwinger Model on $S^2$
summary: The Schwinger model is perhaps the simplest non-trivial exactly-solvable QFT. In this note we examine the perturbative structure of the theory on the sphere and show that its quantum corrections match those predicted by the expansion of the exact solution.

AI.tldr: The paper examines perturbative quantum corrections in the Schwinger model on a sphere and shows they match the exact solution's expansion.
AI.motivation: To verify that perturbative calculations in the Schwinger model (a simple exactly-solvable QFT) on curved spacetime (sphere) correctly reproduce the predictions from the exact non-perturbative solution.
AI.method: Analyzing the perturbative structure of the Schwinger model on a spherical background geometry, comparing quantum corrections from perturbation theory with the expansion of the known exact solution.
AI.result: The perturbative quantum corrections on the sphere match those predicted by expanding the exact solution, confirming consistency between perturbative and non-perturbative approaches.
AI.conclusion: The Schwinger model's perturbative expansion on curved spacetime correctly captures the quantum behavior predicted by the exact solution, validating the perturbative approach for this simple QFT.

title: Hyperbolic form factors for Yukawa interactions, and applications to the Earth
summary:
We define the hyperbolic form factor of a density distribution as its bilateral Laplace transform, related by duality or analytic continuation to its form factor. For a sphere it is given by $Φ(x = kR) =\langle \cosh \vec k.\vec r\rangle=\langle\sinh kr /kr\rangle $, expanded as $\sum \frac{x^{2n}}{(2n+1)!} \frac{\langle r^{2n}\rangle}{R^{2n}} $, and similarly for the form factor $ \langle \sin kr/kr\rangle$. It is also obtained from the bilateral Laplace transform of $2πr\,ρ(|r|)$, and enters in the determination of the outside Yukawa potential induced by a new charge for a mediator of mass $m=k=1/λ$. $Φ(x)$ may be expressed as $\frac{3}{x^3}\,(x \cosh x - \sinh x)\ \barρ(x)/ρ_0$, where $\barρ(x)$ is an effective density decreasing, for $dρ/dr<0$, from the average $ρ_0$ at small $x$, down to $ρ(R)$. An inversion formula allows one to recover $ρ(r)$ from an analytic continuation of $Φ(x)$, as $ρ(r) =ρ_0\,(2R/3πr)\intΦ(ix) \sin (x\frac{r}{R})\,x\,dx$.
  $Φ(x)$ for the Earth is essential to determine limits on a new force, as tested by MICROSCOPE, depending on the density distribution within the Earth. Quite remarkably, much simplified density profiles, such as $ρ= ρ_0\ 2R/3r $ or $ρ= ρ_0\, (\frac54-\frac{r}{R}+ \frac{R}{3r})$, provide analytic expressions of $Φ(x)$ and $\barρ(x)$ giving almost the same values as in a 5-shell model. $\,Φ(x)=(\sinh\frac{x}{2}/\frac{x}{2})^2$ is valid to within $\simeq 1\,\%$ up to $x=4$. $\,Φ(x)= [7x^2\cosh x-24\cosh x+9x\sinh x -4x^2+24]/(4x^4)$ is valid to within 1 % for $λ> $ 100 km (or $m< 2\times 10^{-12}$ eV/$c^2$). For $m=10^{-12}$ eV/$c^2$ the coupling limits are increased by 34 as compared to a massless mediator, to $|g_{B-L}|< 3.6 \times 10^{-24} $ and $|g_B|<2.6\times 10^{-23}$ for a spin-1 mediator, with slightly different limits in the spin-0 case.

AI.tldr: The paper defines hyperbolic form factors for density distributions using bilateral Laplace transforms, applies them to Earth's density to constrain new forces, and finds simplified density profiles yield accurate results comparable to complex 5-shell models.
AI.motivation: To develop mathematical tools for analyzing density distributions through hyperbolic form factors, enabling precise constraints on new fundamental forces (like Yukawa potentials from hypothetical mediators) using Earth's density profile, with applications to experiments like MICROSCOPE.
AI.method: Define hyperbolic form factor Φ(x) as bilateral Laplace transform of density distribution; derive expressions for spheres; develop inversion formula to recover ρ(r) from Φ(x); apply to Earth using simplified analytic density profiles; compare with 5-shell model; compute constraints on new force couplings.
AI.result: Simplified density profiles (ρ=ρ₀2R/3r and ρ=ρ₀(5/4 - r/R + R/3r)) yield Φ(x) expressions accurate to ~1% up to x=4; for λ>100 km (m<2×10⁻¹² eV/c²), accuracy within 1%; for m=10⁻¹² eV/c², coupling limits increase by factor 34 compared to massless mediator: |g_{B-L}|<3.6×10⁻²⁴ and |g_B|<2.6×10⁻²³ for spin-1 mediator.
AI.conclusion: Hyperbolic form factors provide powerful framework for analyzing density distributions; simplified Earth density models yield remarkably accurate results comparable to complex multi-shell models; method enables precise constraints on new fundamental forces from experiments like MICROSCOPE, with significant implications for beyond-Standard-Model physics searches.

title: At the Corner of Quantum and Gravity
comment: 145 pages, 7 figures, submitted in fulfillment of the requirements for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy in the Department BP2, NCBJ, Warsaw
summary: In the presence of spacetime boundaries, diffeomorphisms in gravitational theories can become physical and acquire non-vanishing Noether charges. These charges obey an algebra which, within the extended phase-space formalism, faithfully realizes diffeomorphism algebra. The corner proposal takes this algebra of physical corner symmetries as a fundamental ingredient of quantum gravity, in close analogy with the role of the Poincaré group in quantum field theory. In this thesis we develop the quantum corner framework in the two-dimensional setting. We give the full representation theory of the two-dimensional extended corner symmetry group, which may be interpreted either as the symmetry group of two-dimensional gravity or as the corner symmetry group relevant for four-dimensional spherically symmetric gravity. Within the corner proposal, the resulting representation spaces are then interpreted as candidate Hilbert spaces for quantum gravity. This representation-theoretic structure naturally enables a description of local subsystems. In particular, we present a gluing procedure that constructs quantum states associated with an entangling corner between two spacetime subregions, and use it to compute the entanglement entropy between the two regions. To connect the quantum observables to the classical corner charges, we construct the coadjoint orbits of the quantum corner symmetry group and relate them to the classical structure through twisted moment maps and to the quantum structure through generalized Perelomov coherent states. This provides a notion of semiclassical limit within the corner framework. Finally, in the context of static, spherically symmetric spacetimes, we show that a distinguished family of coherent states reproduces the horizon area law for entropy in the semiclassical limit, yielding a quantum, symmetry-based explanation of the Bekenstein--Hawking formula.

AI.tldr: Thesis develops quantum corner framework for 2D gravity, showing how corner symmetries provide Hilbert spaces for quantum gravity, enable subsystem description with entanglement entropy calculation, and yield Bekenstein-Hawking entropy from coherent states.
AI.motivation: To establish a quantum framework based on the corner proposal, where physical diffeomorphisms at spacetime boundaries provide fundamental symmetries for quantum gravity, analogous to Poincaré group in QFT.
AI.method: Develop representation theory of 2D extended corner symmetry group; construct gluing procedure for entangling corners; relate quantum observables to classical charges via coadjoint orbits, twisted moment maps, and Perelomov coherent states.
AI.result: Full representation theory of 2D corner symmetry group; quantum Hilbert spaces for gravity; entanglement entropy calculation for subsystems; semiclassical limit via coherent states; derivation of Bekenstein-Hawking entropy from horizon area law.
AI.conclusion: The corner symmetry framework provides a viable approach to quantum gravity with natural subsystem description, entanglement structure, and semiclassical limit that recovers known gravitational thermodynamics.

title: B-jet Tagging Using a Hybrid Edge Convolution and Transformer Architecture
summary: Jet flavor tagging plays an important role in precise Standard Model measurement enabling the extraction of mass dependence in jet-quark interaction and quark-gluon plasma (QGP) interactions. They also enable inferring the nature of particles produced in high-energy particle collisions that contain heavy quarks. The classification of bottom jets is vital for exploring new Physics scenarios in proton-proton collisions. In this research, we present a hybrid deep learning architecture that integrates edge convolutions with transformer self-attention mechanisms, into one single architecture called the Edge Convolution Transformer (ECT) model for bottom-quark jet tagging. ECT processes track-level features (impact parameters, momentum, and their significances) alongside jet-level observables (vertex information and kinematics) to achieve state-of-the-art performance. The study utilizes the ATLAS simulation dataset. We demonstrate that ECT achieves 0.9333 AUC for b-jet versus combined charm and light jet discrimination, surpassing ParticleNet (0.8904 AUC) and the pure transformer baseline (0.9216 AUC). The model maintains inference latency below 0.060 ms per jet on modern GPUs, meeting the stringent requirements for real-time event selection at the LHC. Our results demonstrate that hybrid architectures combining local and global features offer superior performance for challenging jet classification tasks. The proposed architecture achieves good results in b-jet tagging, particularly excelling in charm jet rejection (the most challenging task), while maintaining competitive light-jet discrimination comparable to pure transformer models.

AI.tldr: The Edge Convolution Transformer (ECT) model combines edge convolutions with transformer self-attention for bottom-quark jet tagging, achieving state-of-the-art 0.9333 AUC and fast inference suitable for real-time LHC event selection.
AI.motivation: Jet flavor tagging is crucial for Standard Model measurements, studying jet-quark/QGP interactions, and exploring new physics in proton-proton collisions. Bottom jet classification specifically enables investigation of new physics scenarios at the LHC.
AI.method: Hybrid deep learning architecture integrating edge convolutions with transformer self-attention mechanisms (ECT). Processes both track-level features (impact parameters, momentum, significances) and jet-level observables (vertex information, kinematics) using the ATLAS simulation dataset.
AI.result: ECT achieves 0.9333 AUC for b-jet vs. combined charm and light jet discrimination, surpassing ParticleNet (0.8904 AUC) and pure transformer baseline (0.9216 AUC). Maintains inference latency below 0.060 ms per jet on modern GPUs. Excels particularly in charm jet rejection while maintaining competitive light-jet discrimination.
AI.conclusion: Hybrid architectures combining local (edge convolution) and global (transformer) features offer superior performance for challenging jet classification tasks. ECT demonstrates practical viability for real-time event selection at the LHC with state-of-the-art b-jet tagging performance.

title: Correction exponents in the chiral Heisenberg model at $1/N^2$: singular contributions and operator mixing
summary: We calculate the correction exponents in the chiral Heisenberg model in the $1/N$ expansion. These exponents are related to the slopes of $β$ functions at the phase transition point. We present the results at order $1/N^2$ and check that they agree with the results of the $ε$ expansion near $d = 4$. We find that one of the correction exponents diverges as $d \to 3$. We argue that the appearance of the pole is a rather general phenomenon and is associated with operator mixing involving the system of four-fermion operators. After analyzing the operator mixing structure, we propose a resummation procedure which modifies the exponents already at leading order. We also perform calculations directly in the three-dimensional model and find complete agreement with the resummed exponents.

AI.tldr: The paper calculates correction exponents in the chiral Heisenberg model using 1/N expansion, finding agreement with ε-expansion near d=4, discovering a divergent exponent as d→3, analyzing operator mixing, proposing a resummation procedure, and verifying results in 3D.
AI.motivation: To compute correction exponents in the chiral Heisenberg model using 1/N expansion and understand their behavior, particularly the divergence observed as dimension approaches 3, which requires analysis of operator mixing and development of resummation techniques.
AI.method: Uses 1/N expansion up to order 1/N² to calculate correction exponents, compares with ε-expansion near d=4, analyzes operator mixing structure involving four-fermion operators, proposes resummation procedure, and performs direct calculations in three-dimensional model.
AI.result: Found agreement between 1/N² results and ε-expansion near d=4, discovered one correction exponent diverges as d→3, identified pole appearance as general phenomenon related to operator mixing, developed resummation procedure that modifies exponents at leading order, and verified complete agreement between resummed exponents and direct 3D calculations.
AI.conclusion: The divergence of correction exponents as d→3 is a general phenomenon tied to operator mixing of four-fermion operators, requiring resummation procedures that yield consistent results when compared with direct three-dimensional calculations.

title: Sequential retuning of PYTHIA~8.316 to a global soft-QCD basis in pp collisions at $\sqrts=0.9-13$ TeV
summary:
We present a sequential nine-parameter retune of PYTHIA 8.316, built on the Monash 2013 baseline, for soft-QCD observables in proton--proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=0.9$--$13$ TeV. The tune is constructed with direct generator evaluation and developed in stages: an initial five-parameter localization in the hadronization-sensitive sector, successive extensions driven by multi-energy minimum-bias tensions, and a final expansion to a broader soft-QCD fit basis. The fitted set includes minimum-bias charged-particle data, identified-hadron spectra and ratios, underlying-event observables, and event-shape distributions. A separate held-out validation basis is kept outside the fit.
  The final tune retunes nine non-perturbative parameters controlling fragmentation, strangeness suppression, diquark production, color reconnection, MPI regularization and its energy dependence, the impact-parameter overlap profile, and transverse-momentum generation in string breaking. On the common fit basis, the grouped score density improves from $99.18$ for Monash 2013 to $85.67$. The strongest gains occur in the 13 TeV minimum-bias and underlying-event sectors, with further improvement in the ALICE identified-hadron blocks and a smaller gain in the CMS 13 TeV identified-hadron sector. Monash remains better in the CMS 7 TeV underlying-event block and the ATLAS 7 TeV event-shape block, while the low-energy charged-particle sector remains the main unresolved tension for both tunes.
  The held-out validation basis supports the same picture. Monash remains slightly better in the low-energy CMS validation blocks, but the present tune performs better in the ATLAS early underlying-event block and in both held-out 13 TeV charged-particle sectors. We interpret it as a controlled soft-QCD retune that improves a broad set of observables while keeping its limitations explicit.

AI.tldr: A nine-parameter retune of PYTHIA 8.316 improves soft-QCD modeling for pp collisions at 0.9-13 TeV, achieving better overall agreement with data than the Monash 2013 baseline.
AI.motivation: To improve the description of soft-QCD observables in proton-proton collisions across multiple energies (0.9-13 TeV) by systematically retuning non-perturbative parameters in PYTHIA 8.316 beyond the Monash 2013 baseline.
AI.method: Sequential nine-parameter retune constructed through direct generator evaluation in stages: initial five-parameter localization for hadronization, successive extensions driven by multi-energy minimum-bias tensions, and final expansion to broader soft-QCD fit basis including minimum-bias charged-particle data, identified-hadron spectra/ratios, underlying-event observables, and event-shape distributions.
AI.result: Grouped score density improved from 99.18 (Monash 2013) to 85.67 on common fit basis. Strongest gains at 13 TeV minimum-bias and underlying-event sectors, with improvements in ALICE identified-hadron blocks. Monash remains better in CMS 7 TeV underlying-event and ATLAS 7 TeV event-shape blocks. Low-energy charged-particle sector remains unresolved tension for both tunes.
AI.conclusion: The retune provides controlled improvement across broad soft-QCD observables while explicitly acknowledging limitations, particularly in low-energy charged-particle sectors. Validation supports the improvement pattern, making it a systematic enhancement over Monash 2013 for soft-QCD modeling.

title: On gauging Abelian extensions of finite and U(1) groups
comment: 30 pages plus an appendix. Comments are welcome
summary: We consider Abelian extensions of global symmetries of the form $A \to G \to K$, with $A$ finite (and similar higher-group structures). For a quantum field theory $\mathcal{T}$ with symmetry $G$, we compare gauging $G$ directly with gauging first $A$ and then $K$, and show that for finite Abelian groups and for $K \simeq U(1)$ the two procedures are equivalent as expected, $\mathcal{T}/G \simeq \mathcal{T}/A/K$. In the continuous case $K=U(1)$, after gauging the full extension, the dual symmetry $\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}_q^{(d-2)}$ fits into an extension characterizing the topological data of the magnetic $U(1)_m^{(d-3)}$ symmetry. This is better described using differential cohomology. We also briefly comment on the relation to symmetry fractionalization.

AI.tldr: Gauging Abelian symmetry extensions A→G→K yields equivalent results whether done directly (G) or sequentially (A then K), with differential cohomology clarifying topological structure.
AI.motivation: To understand equivalence between direct gauging of symmetry extension G versus sequential gauging of its components A and K, particularly for finite Abelian groups and U(1) cases, and to characterize topological data of resulting dual symmetries.
AI.method: Compare gauging procedures: direct gauging of G versus sequential gauging (first A, then K). Use differential cohomology to describe topological structure of magnetic U(1) symmetry after full gauging. Analyze finite Abelian groups and K=U(1) cases.
AI.result: For finite Abelian groups and K=U(1), the two gauging procedures are equivalent: T/G ≃ T/A/K. After gauging full extension with K=U(1), dual symmetry Ẑ_q^(d-2) fits into extension characterizing topological data of magnetic U(1)_m^(d-3) symmetry.
AI.conclusion: Gauging symmetry extensions can be performed equivalently either directly or sequentially for finite Abelian groups and U(1) cases. Differential cohomology provides proper framework for describing topological structure of resulting magnetic symmetries, with connections to symmetry fractionalization.
