title: From Higgs physics to lepton flavour violation: current bounds and future prospects for vector-like lepton models
summary: We present a comprehensive phenomenological study of a class of six vector-like lepton models with seesaw-like mass contributions and strong modifications to Higgs and lepton phenomenology. We focus on lepton flavour conserving and violating observables across all lepton generations and collider observables like $Z$ and Higgs decays. In light of the recent progress at the LHC and precision measurements such as muon $g-2$, as well as in anticipation of upcoming experiments like MEGII, Mu2e/COMET, Mu3e, Belle II and at the HL-LHC, we systematically survey the viable parameter space and identify patterns and correlations. The considered class of models gives rise to a rich and testable phenomenology with robust and complementary probes that allow to distinguish between models in the coming experimental era.

AI.tldr: Six vector-like lepton models with seesaw-like masses show rich Higgs and lepton phenomenology, analyzed through flavor observables and collider signals in light of current and future experiments.
AI.motivation: To systematically study vector-like lepton models with seesaw-like mass contributions that strongly modify Higgs and lepton phenomenology, motivated by recent LHC progress, precision measurements like muon g-2, and upcoming experiments.
AI.method: Comprehensive phenomenological analysis of six vector-like lepton models with seesaw-like mass contributions, focusing on lepton flavor conserving/violating observables across all generations and collider observables like Z and Higgs decays.
AI.result: Systematic survey of viable parameter space reveals patterns and correlations; models produce rich, testable phenomenology with robust complementary probes to distinguish between models.
AI.conclusion: The considered class of models offers a rich phenomenology with multiple complementary experimental probes that will allow discrimination between different models in the coming experimental era.

title: Nonperturbative Higgs-Schwinger mechanism at the origin of the gluon mass and color confinement
summary: Evidence from lattice and continuum studies supports the existence of a fully nonperturbative Higgs mechanism generating mass for gluons in the gauge sector of the strong interactions in linear covariant gauges. The broken charge is the Kugo-Ojima charge. The corresponding unphysical Goldstone boson is a bound-state superposition of two gluons, three gluons and a ghost-antighost pair. Mass generation occurs via the Schwinger mechanism, triggered by the formation of the Goldstone boson. Once corrected for symmetry breaking, the color charge operator is unbroken and confining.

AI.tldr: Nonperturbative Higgs mechanism generates gluon mass in QCD via Schwinger mechanism, with Kugo-Ojima charge breaking and Goldstone boson formation.
AI.motivation: To explain gluon mass generation in QCD's gauge sector through a nonperturbative mechanism that reconciles with confinement and color charge conservation.
AI.method: Combines lattice and continuum studies to analyze the Higgs mechanism in linear covariant gauges, focusing on Kugo-Ojima charge breaking and Goldstone boson formation via Schwinger mechanism.
AI.result: Evidence supports existence of nonperturbative Higgs mechanism generating gluon mass, with Goldstone boson as bound state of gluons and ghost-antighost pairs, while color charge remains unbroken and confining.
AI.conclusion: Gluon mass generation occurs through Schwinger mechanism triggered by Goldstone boson formation, with Kugo-Ojima charge breaking but color charge operator remaining intact and confining.

title: CayleyPy-4: AI-Holography. Towards analogs of holographic string dualities for AI tasks
summary:
This is the fourth paper in the CayleyPy project, which applies AI methods to the exploration of large graphs. In this work, we suggest the existence of a new discrete version of holographic string dualities for this setup, and discuss their relevance to AI systems and mathematics. Many modern AI tasks -- such as those addressed by GPT-style language models or RL systems -- can be viewed as direct analogues of predicting particle trajectories on graphs. We investigate this problem for a large family of Cayley graphs, for which we show that surprisingly it admits a dual description in terms of discrete strings. We hypothesize that such dualities may extend to a range of AI systems where they can lead to more efficient computational approaches. In particular, string holographic images of states are proposed as natural candidates for data embeddings, motivated by the "complexity = volume" principle in AdS/CFT.
  For Cayley graphs of the symmetric group S_n, our results indicate that the corresponding dual objects are flat, planar polygons. The diameter of the graph is equal to the number of integer points inside the polygon scaled by n. Vertices of the graph can be mapped holographically to paths inside the polygon, and the usual graph distances correspond to the area under the paths, thus directly realising the "complexity = volume" paradigm. We also find evidence for continuous CFTs and dual strings in the large n limit. We confirm this picture and other aspects of the duality in a large initial set of examples. We also present new datasets (obtained by a combination of ML and conventional tools) which should be instrumental in establishing the duality for more general cases.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a discrete holographic string duality for Cayley graphs, connecting AI tasks to string theory concepts, with applications to data embeddings and computational efficiency.
AI.motivation: To explore connections between AI systems and mathematical physics by investigating how modern AI tasks (like those in GPT models and RL systems) can be viewed as analogues of particle trajectory prediction on graphs, and to discover potential dual descriptions that could lead to more efficient computational approaches.
AI.method: Investigates Cayley graphs, particularly for symmetric groups S_n, showing they admit dual descriptions in terms of discrete strings. Uses a combination of ML and conventional tools to generate datasets, maps graph vertices holographically to paths inside polygons, and analyzes graph distances as areas under paths.
AI.result: For Cayley graphs of S_n, dual objects are flat planar polygons where graph diameter equals number of integer points inside polygon scaled by n. Graph vertices map to paths inside polygons with distances corresponding to area under paths, realizing "complexity = volume" paradigm. Evidence found for continuous CFTs and dual strings in large n limit, confirmed through initial examples.
AI.conclusion: Proposes existence of discrete holographic string dualities for Cayley graphs with relevance to AI systems, suggesting string holographic images as natural candidates for data embeddings and potential for more efficient computational approaches in AI through these mathematical physics connections.

title: Recoil corrections to pentaquark molecules with an SU(3) anti-triplet heavy baryon
summary: Recoil corrections, which appear at order $\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{M})$, turn out to be crucial for the pentaquark molecules with heavy flavor. In the past, such corrections were typically regarded as negligible for the formation of heavy molecules. However, our research manifests the important impacts on the spectra of possible baryon-meson bound states. In certain cases, the binding energy sharply decreases after considering the recoil corrections. Using the one-boson-exchange (OBE) model, we have studied a series of double heavy and hidden heavy pentaquark states with an SU(3) anti-triplet baryon, including $Ξ_{c}\bar{D}^{(*)}$, $Λ_{c}\bar{D}^{(*)}$, $Ξ_{c}D^{(*)}$, $Λ_{c}D^{(*)}$, along with their bottom analogues. Considering both the $S$\--{}$D$ wave mixing effect and the recoil corrections, we find that recoil corrections, working against the stability of bound states in certain isospin-singlet channels, which cannot be ignored. For the $Ξ_{c}\bar{D}$ and $Ξ_{c}D$ systems with $I(J^P)=0(\frac{1}{2}^{-})$, the $Ξ_{c}\bar{D}^{*}$ and $Ξ_{c}D^{*}$ systems, as well as their bottom counterparts, with $I(J^P)=0(\frac{1}{2}^{-})$ and $0(\frac{3}{2}^{-})$, and the $Λ_{b}\bar{B}^{*}$ system with $I(J^P)=\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}^{-})$ and $\frac{1}{2}(\frac{3}{2}^{-})$, although the bound state solution can be found both with and without considering the recoil corrections, the inclusion of recoil corrections weakens the attraction of the molecules. This phenomenon arising from recoil corrections is especially prominent in the $Ξ_{c}\bar{D}^{*}$ and $Ξ_{c}D^{*}$ systems.

AI.tldr: Recoil corrections at O(1/M) are crucial for heavy pentaquark molecules, significantly affecting binding energies and stability of baryon-meson bound states in double-heavy and hidden-heavy systems.
AI.motivation: Previous studies typically regarded recoil corrections as negligible for heavy molecule formation, but this research demonstrates their important impacts on spectra of possible baryon-meson bound states, showing they cannot be ignored.
AI.method: Used the one-boson-exchange (OBE) model to study double heavy and hidden heavy pentaquark states with SU(3) anti-triplet baryons, including ΞcD̅(*), ΛcD̅(*), ΞcD(*), ΛcD(*) and their bottom analogues, considering both S-D wave mixing and recoil corrections.
AI.result: Recoil corrections work against stability of bound states in certain isospin-singlet channels, weakening molecular attraction. This effect is especially prominent in ΞcD̅* and ΞcD* systems. Bound state solutions exist both with and without recoil corrections, but inclusion of recoil corrections reduces binding energies.
AI.conclusion: Recoil corrections at O(1/M) are crucial for accurate description of heavy pentaquark molecules and cannot be neglected, as they significantly affect binding energies and stability of baryon-meson bound states in heavy flavor systems.

title: Conditional Wasserstein GAN for Simulating Neutrino Event Summaries using Incident Energy of Electron Neutrinos
summary: Event simulation for electron neutrino interactions plays a foundational role in precision measurements in particle physics experiments, yet the computational demand of traditional Monte Carlo methods remains a significant challenge, especially for complete, high-dimensional event reconstruction. In this study, we present a generative model based on the Conditional Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (CW-GAN) framework. This architecture is conditioned on the input neutrino energy. It utilizes a Wasserstein loss function, stabilized by a gradient penalty, to learn the complex mapping from a latent space to structured kinematic data. Our model is tailored to replicate the full multidimensional kinematics of electron neutrino interactions as described by the GENIE event generator. Our focus is specifically on the Inverse Beta Decay (IBD-CC), Neutral Current (NC), and nue-e-elastic scattering processes (NuEElastic), spanning an energy window of 10-31 MeV. Our approach abandons variable reduction schemes and instead generates the entire summary ntuple, enabling holistic event-by-event modeling. Training is performed separately for each of the three interaction types, with rigorous convergence monitoring over 100-300 epochs per channel. We perform a rigorous quantitative validation against held-out GENIE test datasets. The generated samples demonstrate fidelity, reproducing the 1D marginal distributions for all kinematic variables with statistical compatibility, and successfully capturing the complex non-linear correlations between them. This work offers a scalable and efficient alternative to traditional MC event generation, providing full-spectrum kinematic simulation for key electron neutrino interaction channels while drastically reducing computational overhead.

AI.tldr: CW-GAN generative model for efficient electron neutrino event simulation, reproducing full multidimensional kinematics of IBD-CC, NC, and NuEElastic interactions from 10-31 MeV with statistical fidelity to GENIE generator.
AI.motivation: Traditional Monte Carlo methods for electron neutrino event simulation are computationally demanding, especially for complete high-dimensional event reconstruction. There's a need for scalable and efficient alternatives that can provide full-spectrum kinematic simulation while reducing computational overhead.
AI.method: Conditional Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (CW-GAN) framework conditioned on input neutrino energy, using Wasserstein loss stabilized by gradient penalty. Model learns mapping from latent space to structured kinematic data, generating entire summary ntuple without variable reduction. Training performed separately for three interaction types (IBD-CC, NC, NuEElastic) over 100-300 epochs per channel with rigorous convergence monitoring.
AI.result: Generated samples demonstrate statistical compatibility with held-out GENIE test datasets, reproducing 1D marginal distributions for all kinematic variables and capturing complex non-linear correlations. Model successfully replicates full multidimensional kinematics across the 10-31 MeV energy window for all three interaction channels.
AI.conclusion: CW-GAN offers a scalable, efficient alternative to traditional MC event generation for electron neutrino interactions, providing full-spectrum kinematic simulation while drastically reducing computational overhead, enabling holistic event-by-event modeling without variable reduction schemes.

title: Isospin-breaking effects of the double-charm molecular pentaquarks
summary: We investigate isospin-breaking effects in double-charm molecular pentaquarks with the $D^{(*)}Σ_c^{(*)}$ configuration, using the one-boson-exchange potential framework. In these systems, the isospin-breaking effects arise from two sources: the strong interaction, which manifests as the threshold difference of the $D^{(*)}Σ_c^{(*)}$ components in the same isospin multiplet and the mass splittings of the exchanged isovector mesons ($π$ and $ρ$); and the electromagnetic interaction between charged $D^{(*)}$ and $Σ_c^{(*)}$ components. We calculate the binding properties and the isospin mixing angle between the $I=1/2$ and $I=3/2$ states of the $D^{(*)}Σ_c^{(*)}$ system. Our results show that the isospin-breaking effect contributes a significant correction of roughly $10\%-30\%$ to the binding energy. This effect is particularly pronounced in loosely bound molecular candidates, which are characterized by small binding energies and large root-mean-square radii. We therefore conclude that the explicit inclusion of isospin-breaking effects is essential for achieving the precision in theoretical calculations necessary to match rapidly advancing experimental programs. Our results are expected to provide valuable guidance for future high-precision experimental studies of deuteron-like molecular states.

AI.tldr: Study of isospin-breaking effects in double-charm molecular pentaquarks using one-boson-exchange potential, showing 10-30% binding energy corrections crucial for precision calculations.
AI.motivation: To investigate isospin-breaking effects in double-charm molecular pentaquarks with D^{(*)}Σ_c^{(*)} configurations, as these effects are important for achieving theoretical precision matching advancing experimental programs.
AI.method: Using one-boson-exchange potential framework to calculate binding properties and isospin mixing angle between I=1/2 and I=3/2 states, considering strong interaction effects (threshold differences and meson mass splittings) and electromagnetic interactions between charged components.
AI.result: Isospin-breaking effects contribute significant corrections of 10-30% to binding energy, particularly pronounced in loosely bound molecular candidates with small binding energies and large root-mean-square radii.
AI.conclusion: Explicit inclusion of isospin-breaking effects is essential for achieving theoretical precision necessary to match rapidly advancing experimental programs, providing valuable guidance for future high-precision experimental studies of deuteron-like molecular states.

title: Spacelike and timelike structure functions: a dispersive crossing relation
summary: Crossing symmetry suggests that deep inelastic scattering and semi inclusive electron-positron annihilation are governed by analytic continuations of a single forward amplitude. Drell, Levy, and Yan proposed that the hadronic tensor admits analytic continuation and demonstrated, in reasonable models, that connected contributions to the cross-section continue. They also identified obstructions to continuation of the current correlator. In this work we supplement their observation with a new dispersive proposal for analytic continuation of the correlator and, assuming polynomial boundedness, derive subtracted dispersion relations relating spacelike and timelike cross sections. We introduce a new factorized function that quantifies the obstruction to crossing and compute its hard kernel at lowest order. The resulting identity connects distribution functions in deep inelastic scattering to fragmentation functions in annihilation.

AI.tldr: Analytic continuation connects deep inelastic scattering and semi-inclusive e+e- annihilation via a single forward amplitude, with new dispersive relations derived between spacelike and timelike cross sections.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous analytic continuation between deep inelastic scattering (DIS) and semi-inclusive electron-positron annihilation, addressing the obstructions to continuation of the current correlator identified by Drell, Levy, and Yan.
AI.method: Supplement Drell-Levy-Yan observations with a new dispersive proposal for analytic continuation of the correlator, assuming polynomial boundedness to derive subtracted dispersion relations. Introduce a factorized function quantifying crossing obstruction and compute its hard kernel at lowest order.
AI.result: Derived subtracted dispersion relations connecting spacelike (DIS) and timelike (annihilation) cross sections. Obtained an identity connecting distribution functions in DIS to fragmentation functions in annihilation via the computed hard kernel.
AI.conclusion: Crossing symmetry can be rigorously implemented through analytic continuation with proper treatment of obstructions, establishing a fundamental connection between distribution and fragmentation functions in different scattering processes.

title: Strong decays of the hidden-charm molecular pentaquarks
summary: We investigate the strong decays of the recently observed hidden-charm pentaquarks \(P_ψ^N(4312)\), \(P_ψ^N(4440)\), and \(P_ψ^N(4457)\), as well as \(P_{ψs}^Λ(4338)\) and \(P_{ψs}^Λ(4459)\), within the molecular framework using the effective Lagrangian approach. We construct the effective Lagrangians describing the S-wave couplings between these pentaquarks and their constituent hadrons, namely \(Σ_c\bar{D}^{(*)}\) and \(Ξ_c\bar{D}^{(*)}\), and determine the coupling constants via the residues of the scattering \(T\)-matrix at the bound-state poles. Our results show that the decay widths are sensitive to the cutoff parameters in the form factors, whereas the branching fractions exhibit only weak dependence. Using \(P_ψ^N(4312)\) to calibrate the cutoff range, we further explore the spin assignments of \(P_ψ^N(4440)\) and \(P_ψ^N(4457)\). Our calculations favor the assignment where the lower-mass state \(P_ψ^N(4440)\) carries higher spin \(J = 3/2\) and the higher-mass state \(P_ψ^N(4457)\) carries lower spin \(J = 1/2\). In addition, the experimental widths of \(P_{ψs}^Λ(4338)\) and \(P_{ψs}^Λ(4459)\) can both be well reproduced under the molecular interpretation. We look forward to future experimental analyses with more accumulated data to clarify whether the lineshape of \(P_{ψs}^Λ(4459)\) contains contributions from both spin-\(1/2\) and spin-\(3/2\) states.

AI.tldr: Analysis of hidden-charm pentaquark strong decays using molecular framework and effective Lagrangian approach, determining spin assignments and cutoff parameter sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To investigate the strong decays of recently observed hidden-charm pentaquarks (P_ψ^N(4312), P_ψ^N(4440), P_ψ^N(4457), P_{ψs}^Λ(4338), P_{ψs}^Λ(4459)) within the molecular interpretation framework, determine their spin assignments, and understand their decay properties.
AI.method: Effective Lagrangian approach constructing S-wave couplings between pentaquarks and constituent hadrons (Σ_c\bar{D}^{(*)} and Ξ_c\bar{D}^{(*)}), with coupling constants determined via residues of scattering T-matrix at bound-state poles. Cutoff parameters calibrated using P_ψ^N(4312).
AI.result: Decay widths are sensitive to cutoff parameters in form factors, while branching fractions show weak dependence. Calculations favor spin assignment where P_ψ^N(4440) has J=3/2 and P_ψ^N(4457) has J=1/2. Experimental widths of P_{ψs}^Λ(4338) and P_{ψs}^Λ(4459) are well reproduced under molecular interpretation.
AI.conclusion: The molecular framework successfully describes the strong decays of hidden-charm pentaquarks, provides evidence for specific spin assignments, and suggests that P_{ψs}^Λ(4459) may contain contributions from both spin-1/2 and spin-3/2 states, requiring further experimental investigation.

title: Kinky vortons in the 2HDM
summary: We construct and analyse two-dimensional, current-carrying ring solutions, known as kinky vortons, in the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric global two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM). We demonstrate the existence of multiple dynamically stable configurations that persist under non-axially symmetric perturbations. These solutions are described with high accuracy by the thin string approximation and elastic string formalism, which correctly capture both their equilibrium radii and dynamical oscillation frequencies. Kinky vortons in the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric theory establish the viability of vorton solutions in a phenomenologically motivated extension of the Standard Model, and should provide a computationally tractable proxy for vortons in the $U(1)$-symmetric 2HDM. In addition, we identify a composite domain wall configuration in which localized condensates are supported on secondary domain walls existing on a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ wall, suggesting a mechanism by which kinky-vorton-like defects could arise in a three dimensional setting.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs and analyzes stable 2D current-carrying ring solutions (kinky vortons) in the Z₂-symmetric global two-Higgs-doublet model, demonstrating their dynamical stability and accurate description by thin string approximations.
AI.motivation: To establish the viability of vorton solutions in phenomenologically motivated extensions of the Standard Model, specifically the Z₂-symmetric global two-Higgs-doublet model, and provide a computationally tractable proxy for vortons in U(1)-symmetric 2HDM.
AI.method: Construction and analysis of two-dimensional current-carrying ring solutions using the thin string approximation and elastic string formalism, testing stability under non-axially symmetric perturbations, and identifying composite domain wall configurations.
AI.result: Demonstration of multiple dynamically stable kinky vorton configurations that persist under perturbations, with equilibrium radii and oscillation frequencies accurately captured by thin string approximations; identification of composite domain wall configurations suggesting mechanisms for 3D defect formation.
AI.conclusion: Kinky vortons in Z₂-symmetric 2HDM establish viable vorton solutions in Standard Model extensions and provide a tractable computational proxy for U(1)-symmetric vortons, with composite domain wall configurations suggesting possible 3D defect mechanisms.

title: Multiplicity distribution of produced gluons in deep inelastic scattering: main equations and their homotopy solutions for heavy nuclei
summary: In this paper we discuss the multiplicity distribution in the deep inelastic processes in the frame work of high energy QCD. We obtained three results. First, we get the new derivation of the equations for the cross sections of productions of $n$-cut Pomerons in the final states ($σ_n$). These equations coincide with the equations that have been derived using the Abramovsky, Gribov and Kancheli (AGK) cutting rules but based on the dipole approach to QCD. Second, we developed the homotopy approach for finding the solutions to these equations. It consists with the analytic solution for the first iteration and the converge procedure of calculating the next iterations using computing. Third, we found the analytical solution for $σ_n$ at large $n\,\gtrsim\,N(z) = 2 N_0 \,z\,\exp( z^2/(2 κ))$ with $z = \ln( r^2\,Q^2_s )$. Using this solution we calculate the entropy of the produced gluons at large $z$: $S_E = \ln \left( N(z)\right)$, where the saturation momentum $Q_s$ and all constants are discussed in the text.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a QCD framework for multiplicity distributions in deep inelastic scattering, deriving Pomeron production equations via dipole approach, solving them using homotopy methods, and calculating gluon entropy at high multiplicity.
AI.motivation: To understand multiplicity distributions in deep inelastic processes within high-energy QCD, particularly focusing on n-Pomeron production cross sections and developing analytical solutions for these distributions.
AI.method: Three-pronged approach: 1) Derivation of equations for n-Pomeron production cross sections using dipole approach to QCD, 2) Development of homotopy approach for solving these equations with analytic first iteration and computational convergence, 3) Analytical solution for σ_n at large n using scaling variable z = ln(r²Q_s²).
AI.result: Obtained equations matching AGK cutting rules via dipole approach, developed convergent homotopy solution method, found analytical solution for σ_n at large n, and calculated gluon entropy S_E = ln(N(z)) at large z where N(z) = 2N₀z exp(z²/(2κ)).
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a consistent QCD framework for multiplicity distributions, provides new solution methods for Pomeron production equations, and derives entropy scaling behavior for produced gluons in high-energy deep inelastic scattering.

title: Energy loss predicts no $v_2$ in small systems
summary: We present high-$p_T$ $R_{AB}$ and $v_2$ from a perturbative quantum chromodynamics-based energy loss model that includes event-by-event hydrodynamic evolution of the medium and small system size corrections to the energy loss. The model is calibrated on, and describes well, large system $R_{AA}$ and $v_2$ experimental data. The extrapolation of our model to $\mathrm{Ne}+\mathrm{Ne}$ and $\mathrm{O}+\mathrm{O}$ agrees quantitatively with recent experimental measurements of $R_{AA}$. Surprisingly, at high-$p_T$ our energy loss model predicts $v_2\approx0$ for all symmetric and asymmetric small systems when extracted using either hard-hard or hard-soft two-particle correlations. We argue that all energy loss models will in general predict $v_2\approx0$ when extracted using hard-soft correlations, which is the usual experimental method for measuring anisotropy in hadronic collisions, due to a generic geometric decorrelation between the hard and soft sector participant planes.

AI.tldr: High-pT R_AA and v2 predictions from pQCD energy loss model with event-by-event hydrodynamics show v2≈0 in small systems due to geometric decorrelation between hard and soft sector participant planes.
AI.motivation: To understand jet quenching and collectivity in small collision systems (Ne+Ne, O+O) using a calibrated pQCD energy loss model that successfully describes large system data.
AI.method: Perturbative QCD-based energy loss model incorporating event-by-event hydrodynamic evolution of the medium and small system size corrections to energy loss, calibrated on large system R_AA and v2 data.
AI.result: Model quantitatively agrees with recent experimental R_AA measurements in Ne+Ne and O+O collisions, but predicts v2≈0 at high-pT for all symmetric/asymmetric small systems when using hard-hard or hard-soft correlations.
AI.conclusion: All energy loss models generally predict v2≈0 in small systems when using hard-soft correlations due to geometric decorrelation between hard and soft sector participant planes, challenging conventional interpretations of collectivity.

title: Gravitational waves from holographic first-order QCD phase transition with magnetic field
summary: In this paper, we investigate the generation of gravitational waves (GWs) from a first-order QCD confinement-deconfinement phase transition under external magnetic field from holography. We analyze the GWs spectra across both hard wall and soft wall models for Jouguet detonations and non-runaway scenarios. Our results indicate that increasing the magnetic field shifts the spectral peak to lower frequencies. The predicted GWs signals are potentially detectable by observatories such as IPTA, SKA, BBO and NANOGrav. Decomposing the spectra reveals that sound waves typically dominate the signal around the peak frequency, bubble collisions prevail at spectral extremities, and the contribution from MHD turbulence is significant only for non-runaway bubble scenarios at high frequencies. This work suggests that magnetized QCD phase transitions are viable cosmological sources for observable GW backgrounds, offering a potential pathway to constrain primordial magnetic fields through future PTA observations.

AI.tldr: Holographic study shows magnetic fields shift GW spectra from QCD phase transitions to lower frequencies, potentially detectable by PTAs and offering constraints on primordial magnetic fields.
AI.motivation: To investigate gravitational wave generation from first-order QCD confinement-deconfinement phase transitions under external magnetic fields using holographic methods, and assess detectability by current/future observatories.
AI.method: Holographic analysis using both hard wall and soft wall models for Jouguet detonations and non-runaway scenarios, with decomposition of GW spectra contributions from different sources.
AI.result: Increasing magnetic field shifts spectral peak to lower frequencies; sound waves dominate around peak, bubble collisions at extremities, MHD turbulence significant only for non-runaway scenarios at high frequencies; signals potentially detectable by IPTA, SKA, BBO, NANOGrav.
AI.conclusion: Magnetized QCD phase transitions are viable cosmological sources for observable GW backgrounds, offering potential pathway to constrain primordial magnetic fields through future PTA observations.

title: A Fast Method for Correlated Updates of Proton PDFs and the Strong Coupling $α_s$
summary: We present an extended version of the \texttt{ePump} framework that enables the simultaneous profiling of proton parton distribution functions (PDFs) and the strong coupling $α_s$ using new experimental data. By promoting $α_s$ to a fit parameter within the Hessian updating formalism, the method performs coherent updates of $\{\text{PDFs},α_s\}$ while preserving parameter correlations and the full covariance structure. Validation studies based on CTEQ-TEA analyses with collider data demonstrate that the upgraded \texttt{ePump} accurately reproduces the shifts in PDFs, the preferred $α_s(m_Z)$, and the associated uncertainty reductions obtained in full global fits, including those inferred from Lagrange--Multiplier scans; small deviations arise only for data sets whose $χ^2$ profiles exhibit nonlinear behavior. Applications to representative collider measurements illustrate the impact on the gluon distribution and on precision observables such as the Higgs boson production cross section via gluon fusion. This enhanced framework provides a fast and reliable tool for assessing the effects of new data on the global QCD parameter space, offering near-global-fit accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost.

AI.tldr: Extended ePump framework enables simultaneous profiling of proton PDFs and α_s using new data, providing fast updates with near-global-fit accuracy at reduced computational cost.
AI.motivation: Need for efficient method to simultaneously update proton parton distribution functions (PDFs) and strong coupling α_s using new experimental data while preserving parameter correlations and covariance structure, avoiding computationally expensive full global fits.
AI.method: Extended Hessian updating formalism that promotes α_s to a fit parameter, performing coherent updates of {PDFs, α_s} while maintaining full parameter correlations and covariance structure within the ePump framework.
AI.result: Validation studies with CTEQ-TEA analyses show the upgraded ePump accurately reproduces PDF shifts, preferred α_s(m_Z) values, and uncertainty reductions from full global fits; small deviations only occur for datasets with nonlinear χ² profiles. Applications demonstrate impact on gluon distribution and precision observables like Higgs boson production cross section.
AI.conclusion: The enhanced ePump framework provides a fast, reliable tool for assessing new data effects on global QCD parameter space, offering near-global-fit accuracy at significantly reduced computational cost for simultaneous PDF and α_s profiling.

title: Jet quenching and its substructure dependence due to color decoherence
summary: Motivated by color coherence and decoherence effects in the QCD medium, we propose a theoretical framework that combines vacuum-like emissions and medium-induced radiation to study jet quenching and its dependence on jet cone sizes and substructure. In our approach, a jet produced at a hard scale $Q$ first undergoes vacuum-like evolution, as described by the well-established generating-function method in the double logarithmic approximation. These vacuum-like emissions generate subjets at an infrared momentum scale $Q_0$. Each subjet then experiences medium-induced energy loss as described by the BDMPS-Z formalism. By modeling the QCD bulk medium using OSU (2+1)-dimensional viscous hydrodynamics and treating $Q_0$ together with the jet-quenching parameters at the initial proper time of the hydrodynamic evolution as free parameters, our approach provides a very good description of the inclusive jet modification factor $R_{AA}$ for large-radius jets and its dependence on jet substructure in 0-10% PbPb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\rm{TeV}$, as measured by the ATLAS experiment.

AI.tldr: A theoretical framework combining vacuum-like emissions and medium-induced radiation successfully describes jet quenching and substructure dependence in heavy-ion collisions.
AI.motivation: To understand color coherence and decoherence effects in the QCD medium and develop a comprehensive framework for studying jet quenching dependence on jet cone sizes and substructure.
AI.method: Combines vacuum-like emissions (using generating-function method in double logarithmic approximation) with medium-induced radiation (BDMPS-Z formalism), modeling QCD medium with OSU (2+1)-dimensional viscous hydrodynamics, with Q₀ and initial jet-quenching parameters as free parameters.
AI.result: Provides excellent description of inclusive jet modification factor R_AA for large-radius jets and its dependence on jet substructure in 0-10% PbPb collisions at √s_NN = 5.02 TeV, matching ATLAS experimental data.
AI.conclusion: The combined framework successfully captures both vacuum-like and medium-induced jet evolution, offering a comprehensive description of jet quenching phenomena in heavy-ion collisions.

title: A perturbative framework to probe infrared sensitivity in non-Abelian gauge theories
summary: Understanding the infrared sensitivity of perturbative predictions in QCD is important for assessing the magnitude of possible non-perturbative power corrections to processes with large momentum transfer. In renormalon models, this sensitivity can be related to computable dependences of perturbative quantities on a small gluon mass. However, this procedure cannot be applied to collider processes with gluons at the Born level. To address this problem, we promote the gluon mass to a parameter of a consistent non-Abelian quantum field theory where the gauge symmetry is spontaneously broken through the Higgs mechanism. Working in the limit in which the gluon mass $m_\mathrm{g}$ is the smallest dimensionful parameter, we compute through two loops the $\mathcal{O}(m_\mathrm{g})$ contributions to the relation between the pole and $\overline{\rm MS}$ masses of a heavy quark and to the relation between corresponding field counterterms. We expect that the proposed framework will provide a useful laboratory for probing linear infrared sensitivity of collider observables in QCD.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a consistent quantum field theory framework with spontaneously broken gauge symmetry to study infrared sensitivity in QCD, computing two-loop O(m_g) contributions to heavy quark mass relations and field counterterms.
AI.motivation: To address the limitation of renormalon models in studying infrared sensitivity for collider processes with gluons at Born level, by creating a consistent theoretical framework where gluon mass is a parameter in a spontaneously broken gauge theory.
AI.method: Promote gluon mass to a parameter in a consistent non-Abelian quantum field theory with spontaneously broken gauge symmetry via Higgs mechanism. Work in the limit where gluon mass is smallest dimensionful parameter and compute O(m_g) contributions through two loops for heavy quark pole-MS mass relations and field counterterms.
AI.result: Computed through two loops the O(m_g) contributions to the relation between pole and MS masses of heavy quarks and to corresponding field counterterms in the proposed framework.
AI.conclusion: The developed framework provides a useful laboratory for probing linear infrared sensitivity of collider observables in QCD, overcoming limitations of traditional renormalon models for processes with gluons at Born level.

title: The energy-momentum tensor in a classical model of the electron
summary: We show that the leading non-analytic terms in the small-t expansion of the energy momentum tensor (EMT) form factors of an electrically charged particle in QED can be correctly derived in a classical model of the electron by Bialynicki-Birula. Based on the lucidity of the employed exactly solvable model, we comment also on the recently proposed concept of a regularized proton D-term.

AI.tldr: Classical electron model correctly reproduces leading non-analytic terms in EMT form factors; provides insights on regularized proton D-term concept.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that classical models can capture key quantum field theory features of energy momentum tensor form factors in QED, specifically the leading non-analytic terms in the small momentum transfer expansion.
AI.method: Uses the exactly solvable classical model of the electron by Bialynicki-Birula to compute EMT form factors and compare with QED results, focusing on small momentum transfer expansion.
AI.result: The classical model correctly reproduces the leading non-analytic terms in the small-t expansion of EMT form factors for an electrically charged particle in QED.
AI.conclusion: Classical models can capture essential quantum features of EMT form factors; provides critical perspective on the recently proposed concept of a regularized proton D-term.

title: Landau Damping of Collective Neutrino Oscillation Waves
summary: Dense neutrino media in core-collapse supernovae and neutron star mergers can experience collective flavor transformations in the form of neutrino oscillation waves. It was recently reported that the stable fast modes of collective oscillations can be damped through a mechanism similar to the Landau damping of plasma waves. In this work, we show that the actual damping rates of fast oscillation waves are usually very small and vanishes in the pure fast limit. This result does not affect the unstable modes that eventually drive collective neutrino flavor conversions in supernovae and neutron star mergers.

AI.tldr: Fast neutrino oscillation waves in dense astrophysical media experience minimal damping, with rates approaching zero in pure fast limit, while unstable modes driving flavor conversions remain unaffected.
AI.motivation: To clarify the actual damping behavior of fast collective neutrino oscillation modes in dense astrophysical environments like supernovae and neutron star mergers, addressing recent reports of Landau-like damping mechanisms.
AI.method: Analysis of damping rates for fast oscillation waves in dense neutrino media, examining the pure fast limit behavior and comparing with unstable modes driving flavor conversions.
AI.result: Damping rates of fast oscillation waves are found to be very small and vanish in the pure fast limit, contrasting with earlier suggestions of significant Landau-like damping.
AI.conclusion: The minimal damping of fast modes does not impact the unstable modes responsible for collective neutrino flavor conversions in astrophysical environments, maintaining the significance of these conversion mechanisms.
